description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Under Rule 020101, appointments to offices in the Federal Civil Service are made on whose authority?
option_a: The Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020101, appointments to offices in the Federal Civil Service are made on the authority of the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which of the following is one mode of making appointments under Rule 020101?
option_a: By letter written under the direction of the Federal Civil Service Commission
option_b: By verbal instruction from a colleague
option_d: By personal approval of the applicant
correct_answer: By letter written under the direction of the Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020101, appointments may be made by letter written under the direction of the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Apart from appointment by letter, how else may appointment be made under Rule 020101?
option_a: By informal oral promise only
option_c: By formal agreement between the Officer and the Federal Government or its appointed agents
correct_answer: By formal agreement between the Officer and the Federal Government or its appointed agents
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020101, appointments may also be made by formal agreement between the Officer and the Federal Government or its appointed agents.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Subject to Rules 020205, 020206 and 020207, who may appoint eligible candidates to delegated posts?
option_a: Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
correct_answer: Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020101, Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices are authorized to appoint eligible candidates to posts where the powers of appointment have been delegated to them, subject to Rules 020205, 020206 and 020207.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Under Rule 020102, the Federal Civil Service Commission makes appointments to posts graded within which range?
option_a: GL. 01–06 only
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020102, the Federal Civil Service Commission makes appointments to posts graded GL. 07–17.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Appointments by the Federal Civil Service Commission under Rule 020102 are made when?
option_a: Only when there are available vacancies and the need arises
option_c: Only when a Staff Union requests it
correct_answer: Only when there are available vacancies and the need arises
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102, appointments to GL. 07–17 are made as the need arises into available vacancies after advertisement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Where must vacancies be advertised under Rule 020102?
option_a: In three national newspapers and the Commission’s website
option_b: In one private notice board only
correct_answer: In three national newspapers and the Commission’s website
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102, advertisement shall be in three national newspapers and on the Federal Civil Service Commission’s website.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What is the deadline for submission of applications after placement of advertisement under Rule 020102?
option_a: Two weeks
correct_answer: Six weeks
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102, the deadline for submission of applications from interested candidates is six weeks from the date of placement of the advertisement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Under Rule 020102, each Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office selects candidates from what source?
option_a: The pool of successful candidates at the Civil Service Examination
correct_answer: The pool of successful candidates at the Civil Service Examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102, each Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office selects from the pool of successful candidates at the Civil Service Examination prescribed in Rule 020102(iv).

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Who participates in the appropriate Committees of each Ministry under Rule 020102?
option_a: Representatives of the Federal Civil Service Commission and the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: Representatives of the Federal Civil Service Commission and the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102, the process is handled by the appropriate Committees of each Ministry with representatives of the Federal Civil Service Commission and the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation at the meetings.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What examination is established under Rule 020102 for posts graded GL. 07–10?
option_a: Annual competitive Public/Civil Service Entry Examination
option_c: Promotion interview for retired Officers only
option_d: Private aptitude test by a contractor
correct_answer: Annual competitive Public/Civil Service Entry Examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102(iv), there shall be an annual competitive Public/Civil Service Entry Examination for posts graded GL. 07–10.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: The annual competitive Public/Civil Service Entry Examination under Rule 020102 is for whom?
option_a: New entrants and serving Officers wishing to transfer from other Scheduled Services
correct_answer: New entrants and serving Officers wishing to transfer from other Scheduled Services
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102(iv), the examination is for new entrants and serving Officers wishing to transfer from other Scheduled Services.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Who conducts the annual competitive Public/Civil Service Entry Examination under Rule 020102?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission in conjunction with OHCSF, ASCON and PSIN
option_c: The Federal Ministry of Finance alone
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission in conjunction with OHCSF, ASCON and PSIN
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102(iv), the examination is conducted by the Federal Civil Service Commission in conjunction with the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, ASCON and PSIN.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: To qualify for the examination under Rule 020102, candidates must possess what?
option_a: Qualifications in relevant disciplines as provided in the approved Schemes of Service
correct_answer: Qualifications in relevant disciplines as provided in the approved Schemes of Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102(v), candidates must possess the qualifications in relevant disciplines as provided in the approved Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Who makes the final recommendation under Rule 020102 after the examination process?
option_a: The line Ministries or Extra-Ministerial Offices
option_d: The newspaper that carried the advert
correct_answer: The line Ministries or Extra-Ministerial Offices
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020102(v), final recommendation is made by the line Ministries or Extra-Ministerial Offices in line with their requirements.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Under Rule 020103, who appoints Junior Staff on GL. 06 and below?
option_a: Each Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office
option_b: The Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs only
correct_answer: Each Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020103, each Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office appoints Junior Staff on GL. 06 and below.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which committee handles appointment of Junior Staff under Rule 020103?
option_a: Junior Staff Committee
correct_answer: Junior Staff Committee
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020103, appointment of Junior Staff on GL. 06 and below is handled by the Junior Staff Committee of each Ministry or Office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Under Rule 020103, appointments in Federal Ministries or Extra-Ministerial Offices located in States/Zones shall be from whom?
option_a: Residents of those States/Zones who possess the prescribed qualifications
option_b: Only persons from the Federal Capital Territory
correct_answer: Residents of those States/Zones who possess the prescribed qualifications
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020103, appointments in Federal Ministries or Extra-Ministerial Offices located in States/Zones shall be from residents of those States/Zones who possess the qualifications prescribed in the approved Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: The qualifications required for State/Zone appointments under Rule 020103 must be those prescribed where?
option_a: In the approved Schemes of Service
correct_answer: In the approved Schemes of Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020103, residents of the relevant States/Zones must possess the qualifications prescribed in the approved Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What is the incremental date of an Officer appointed or promoted to a post in the Federal Public Service?
option_a: 1st January of every year
correct_answer: 1st January of every year
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020104, the incremental date of an Officer appointed or promoted to a post in the Federal Public Service is 1st January of every year.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Before enjoying increment under Rule 020104, how long must an Officer have spent on the grade?
option_a: At least six months
correct_answer: At least six months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020104, an Officer must have spent at least six months on the grade before enjoying the increment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What additional condition is required before an Officer enjoys increment under Rule 020104?
option_a: Good performance
correct_answer: Good performance
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020104, an Officer must have spent at least six months on the grade with good performance before enjoying increment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Under Rule 020105, seniority in any Department is determined by what?
option_a: Entry date or date of assumption of duty and/or date of present appointment
option_d: The Officer’s state of origin only
correct_answer: Entry date or date of assumption of duty and/or date of present appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020105, seniority in any Department is determined by the entry date/date of assumption of duty certified by an authorized Officer and/or date of present appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: The date used for seniority under Rule 020105 must be certified by whom?
option_a: An authorized Officer
correct_answer: An authorized Officer
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020105, the entry date or date of assumption of duty used to determine seniority must be certified by an authorized Officer.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Seniority under Rule 020105 is reflected in what records?
option_a: The appropriate register and career progression of the Officers
correct_answer: The appropriate register and career progression of the Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020105, seniority is determined by the relevant dates as reflected in the appropriate register and career progression of the Officers.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What does Rule 020106 provide about unpaid staff?
option_a: The employment of unpaid Staff is prohibited
option_b: Unpaid Staff may be employed freely
option_c: Unpaid Staff are compulsory in all MDAs
option_d: Unpaid Staff must replace paid Officers
correct_answer: The employment of unpaid Staff is prohibited
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020106, the employment of unpaid Staff is prohibited.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020106?
option_a: No unpaid Staff should be employed in the Federal Public Service
option_b: Unpaid Staff may be employed without records
option_d: Unpaid Staff may replace confirmed Officers
correct_answer: No unpaid Staff should be employed in the Federal Public Service
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020106 prohibits the employment of unpaid Staff.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Who must keep an up-to-date record of every Officer under their control?
option_a: Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
correct_answer: Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rule 020107, Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices shall keep an up-to-date record of every Officer under their control.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which form is used for staff records under Rule 020107?
option_a: Form Gen. 60
correct_answer: Form Gen. 60
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107, Staff Record Form Gen. 60 shall be used for personnel records.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Within what period must one copy of Form Gen. 60 be sent to the specified offices under Rule 020107?
option_a: Within one month of the appointment
correct_answer: Within one month of the appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107, one copy of Form Gen. 60 must be sent to the specified offices within one month of the appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which office is among those to receive a copy of Form Gen. 60 under Rule 020107?
option_a: National Record Centre in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: National Record Centre in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107, one copy of Form Gen. 60 must be sent to the National Record Centre in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, among other listed offices.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which of the following offices is also listed to receive Form Gen. 60 under Rule 020107?
option_a: The Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107, Form Gen. 60 is to be sent to the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, among other specified offices.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Form Gen. 60 must be completed in what manner under Rule 020107?
option_a: In ink
correct_answer: In ink
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107, Form Gen. 60 shall be completed in ink.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What does Rule 020107 provide about date of birth recorded on appointment?
option_a: It shall not be changed throughout the Officer’s career
option_b: It may be changed every year
option_c: It is irrelevant to the Officer’s record
option_d: It must be deleted after confirmation
correct_answer: It shall not be changed throughout the Officer’s career
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107(ii), the date of birth recorded on appointment by an Officer shall not be changed throughout the career of the Officer.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: What is the consequence of contravening the date of birth rule under Rule 020107?
option_a: It is regarded as an act of serious misconduct
option_c: It is treated as annual leave
correct_answer: It is regarded as an act of serious misconduct
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020107(ii), contravention of the rule on date of birth recorded on appointment is regarded as an act of serious misconduct.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 1.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 1 of the PSR?
option_a: It covers general appointment authority, FCSC appointments, junior staff appointments, incremental date, seniority, prohibition of unpaid staff and personnel records
option_b: It deals only with medical treatment abroad
option_c: It deals only with burial expenses
option_d: It deals only with disciplinary dismissal
correct_answer: It covers general appointment authority, FCSC appointments, junior staff appointments, incremental date, seniority, prohibition of unpaid staff and personnel records
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 1, Rules 020101 to 020107 cover general appointment provisions, including authority for appointments, FCSC appointments, junior staff appointments, incremental date, seniority, prohibition of unpaid staff and personnel records.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020201, what does recruitment mean?
option_a: Promotion of Officers already in the same Ministry
option_b: Transfer of Officers from State Public Service only
option_c: Filling of vacancies by direct appointment of persons not already in any Public Service of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
option_d: Posting of confirmed Officers within the same Department
correct_answer: Filling of vacancies by direct appointment of persons not already in any Public Service of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 2, Rule 020201, recruitment means filling vacancies by direct appointment of persons not already in any Public Service of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which process is expressly excluded from the definition of recruitment under Rule 020201?
option_a: Direct appointment of new entrants
option_b: Filling vacancies in the Federal Public Service
option_c: Transfer of Officers from other Public Service in the Federation to the Federal Public Service
option_d: Appointment of persons not already in Public Service
correct_answer: Transfer of Officers from other Public Service in the Federation to the Federal Public Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020201, recruitment excludes the transfer of Officers from other Public Service in the Federation to the Federal Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Recruitment under Rule 020201 applies to persons with what status?
option_a: Persons not already in any Public Service of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
option_b: Only Officers already transferred from another Public Service
option_d: Only Officers already confirmed in the Federal Civil Service
correct_answer: Persons not already in any Public Service of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020201 defines recruitment as direct appointment of persons not already in any Public Service of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which of the following is a category of appointment into the Federal Public Service under Rule 020202?
option_a: Appointment as trainees or pupils
correct_answer: Appointment as trainees or pupils
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 2, Rule 020202, appointment into the Federal Public Service may be as trainees or pupils.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which appointment category under Rule 020202 relates to a pensionable post?
option_a: Acting appointment only
option_c: Appointment on probation in a pensionable post
correct_answer: Appointment on probation in a pensionable post
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020202 lists appointment on probation in a pensionable post as one of the categories of appointment into the Federal Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which of the following is listed as a type of appointment under Rule 020202?
option_a: Non-pensionable contract
correct_answer: Non-pensionable contract
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020202, appointment into the Federal Public Service may be on non-pensionable contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which option correctly lists categories of appointment under Rule 020202?
option_a: Trainee or pupil, probation in a pensionable post, non-pensionable contract, acting appointment and special appointment
option_b: Annual leave, maternity leave, sick leave and casual leave
correct_answer: Trainee or pupil, probation in a pensionable post, non-pensionable contract, acting appointment and special appointment
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020202 lists these categories of appointment: trainee or pupil, probation in a pensionable post, non-pensionable contract, acting appointment and special appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: How should Ministries and Extra-Ministerial Offices treat appointments made by the FCSC to NYSC Presidential Merit Award winners?
option_a: They may reject them because of vacancy constraints
option_b: They shall accept them because employment is automatic regardless of vacancy constraints
option_c: They must convert them to unpaid staff
option_d: They must wait until the next leave year
correct_answer: They shall accept them because employment is automatic regardless of vacancy constraints
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020202, Ministries and Extra-Ministerial Offices shall accept appointments made by the Federal Civil Service Commission to NYSC Presidential Merit Award winners whose employment is automatic regardless of vacancy constraints.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What percentage of all recruitments in the Service is reserved for persons with disability under Rule 020202?
option_a: One percent
correct_answer: Five percent
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020202, five percent of all recruitments in the Service shall be reserved for persons with disability.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What should normally happen where posts prove difficult to fill from within the Service?
option_a: They should normally be advertised
option_c: They should be filled only by relatives of serving Officers
option_d: They should be left vacant permanently
correct_answer: They should normally be advertised
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020203, where posts prove difficult to fill from within the Service, they shall normally be advertised.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 020203 mainly addresses what situation?
option_a: Posts difficult to fill from within the Service
correct_answer: Posts difficult to fill from within the Service
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020203 provides that posts which prove difficult to fill from within the Service shall normally be advertised.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: When may a candidate be appointed as a trainee or pupil under Rule 020204?
option_a: Where the candidate requires additional professional experience before being regarded as fully qualified for appointment
option_b: Where the candidate has already retired from Service
option_c: Where the candidate refuses to meet qualification requirements
option_d: Where the candidate is being disciplined
correct_answer: Where the candidate requires additional professional experience before being regarded as fully qualified for appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(a), a candidate may be appointed as trainee or pupil where he requires additional professional experience before he can be regarded as fully qualified for appointment to a specific post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the normal service period for a trainee or pupil under Rule 020204?
option_a: Six months
correct_answer: Two years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(a), a trainee or pupil is appointed for a normal service period of two years in the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Can the normal two-year trainee or pupil period be reduced?
option_a: Yes, in special circumstances
option_b: No, it can never be reduced
correct_answer: Yes, in special circumstances
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(a), the normal two-year trainee or pupil period may be reduced in special circumstances.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: After completing the trainee period, what may happen to the pupil under Rule 020204?
option_a: He may be appointed to the full grade on probation
correct_answer: He may be appointed to the full grade on probation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(a), on completion of the trainee period, the pupil may be appointed to the full grade on probation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: After appointment to full grade on probation, when is the former trainee eligible for confirmation?
option_a: Only after fulfilling the conditions laid down in Rule 020302 where applicable
option_d: Only after refusing the prescribed examination
correct_answer: Only after fulfilling the conditions laid down in Rule 020302 where applicable
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(a), the pupil appointed to the full grade on probation is not eligible for confirmation until he has fulfilled the conditions laid down in Rule 020302 where applicable.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: How is a confirmed Officer advanced to a training grade for experience treated under Rule 020204?
option_a: As if he had been seconded to the training grade
correct_answer: As if he had been seconded to the training grade
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(b), a confirmed Officer advanced to a training grade for necessary experience to qualify for substantive promotion to a senior post is treated as if he had been seconded thereto.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: The secondment period for a confirmed Officer advanced to a training grade should not normally exceed what?
option_a: The period laid down for the training
correct_answer: The period laid down for the training
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(b), the period of secondment will not normally exceed the period laid down for the training except with the special advice of the OHCSF.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Whose special advice may allow the training-grade secondment period to exceed the normal training period?
option_a: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020204(b), extension beyond the normal training period may occur only with the special advice of the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Except where the FCSC decides otherwise, how are first appointments to pensionable establishment treated?
option_a: They are treated as automatic retirement
option_b: They are treated as appointments on probation
option_c: They are treated as unpaid appointments
option_d: They are treated as disciplinary postings
correct_answer: They are treated as appointments on probation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020205, except where the Federal Civil Service Commission decides otherwise, all first appointments to pensionable establishment in posts other than trainee posts will be on probation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which first appointments are excluded from the probation rule in Rule 020205?
option_a: Trainee posts
correct_answer: Trainee posts
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020205, first appointments to pensionable establishment other than trainee posts are on probation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: An Officer confirmed in a lower pensionable post and converted to a higher post is treated how under Rule 020205?
option_a: He is not regarded as on probation in the higher post
option_b: He must start probation again automatically
option_d: He is deemed to have resigned
correct_answer: He is not regarded as on probation in the higher post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020205, an Officer confirmed in a lower pensionable post is not regarded as on probation in a higher post to which he is converted.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the minimum age for eligibility for appointment into the Federal Public Service under Rule 020206?
option_a: 18 years
correct_answer: 18 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(a), every applicant for appointment into the Federal Public Service must not be less than 18 years of age.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the maximum age for eligibility for appointment into the Federal Public Service under Rule 020206?
option_a: 45 years
correct_answer: 50 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(a), every applicant must not be more than 50 years of age.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which qualification requirement is stated under Rule 020206?
option_a: Minimum qualification specified in the Schemes of Service including computer proficiency or literacy
option_b: Only a verbal recommendation from a friend
correct_answer: Minimum qualification specified in the Schemes of Service including computer proficiency or literacy
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(b), an applicant must possess the minimum qualification specified in the Schemes of Service, including computer proficiency or literacy.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What medical condition must an applicant satisfy under Rule 020206?
option_a: He must be certified medically fit for Public Service by an authorized Healthcare Provider
option_c: He must provide only a private family note
option_d: He must submit only an annual leave form
correct_answer: He must be certified medically fit for Public Service by an authorized Healthcare Provider
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(c), an applicant must be certified by an authorized Healthcare Provider as medically fit for Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: What testimonial is required from an applicant under Rule 020206?
option_a: Testimonial of good conduct from last employer or, if not previously employed, from the last school or college attended
option_b: Testimonial from a political campaign office only
option_c: Testimonial from a private travel agent
option_d: Testimonial from a market association only
correct_answer: Testimonial of good conduct from last employer or, if not previously employed, from the last school or college attended
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(d), an applicant must possess a testimonial of good conduct from the last employer or, if not previously employed, from the last school or college attended.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020206, requisite qualifications must be as provided where?
option_a: In the Schemes of Service
correct_answer: In the Schemes of Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(e), an applicant must possess requisite qualifications as provided for in the Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 1 of 2.
question: No Officer shall be appointed into the Federal Public Service without what under Rule 020206?
option_a: Authorized establishment and recruitment waiver from the OHCSF
correct_answer: Authorized establishment and recruitment waiver from the OHCSF
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020206(f), no Officer shall be appointed into the Federal Public Service without authorized establishment and recruitment waiver from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: When is prior specific approval required before appointing a candidate under Rule 020207?
option_a: If the candidate has been convicted of a criminal offence
option_b: If the candidate has never worked before
option_c: If the candidate has a leave address
option_d: If the candidate is below retirement age
correct_answer: If the candidate has been convicted of a criminal offence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(a)(i), no candidate shall be appointed without prior specific approval if the candidate has been convicted of a criminal offence.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Prior specific approval is also required if a candidate was previously employed in Public Service and what happened?
option_a: He was dismissed or called upon to resign or retire
correct_answer: He was dismissed or called upon to resign or retire
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(a)(ii), prior specific approval is required if the candidate was previously employed in Public Service and dismissed or called upon to resign or retire.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who gives prior specific approval under Rule 020207 for the Federal Public Service?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(a), prior specific approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission is required in the listed cases.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who gives prior specific approval in the case of Parastatals under Rule 020207?
option_a: Board or Council
correct_answer: Board or Council
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(a), in the case of Parastatals, prior specific approval of the Board or Council is required in the listed cases.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Must prior specific approval be obtained even where appointment powers have been delegated?
option_a: Yes, it must always be obtained irrespective of any delegation of the Commission’s powers
option_b: No, delegation removes the need for approval
option_c: Only if the Officer is on annual leave
option_d: Only if the candidate requests it
correct_answer: Yes, it must always be obtained irrespective of any delegation of the Commission’s powers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(a), such approval must always be obtained irrespective of any delegation of the Commission’s powers.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Every applicant for Government employment must state whether he has done what?
option_a: Been convicted of a criminal offence
correct_answer: Been convicted of a criminal offence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(b)(i), every applicant for employment by Government must state whether he has been convicted of a criminal offence.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020207, what employment information must every applicant state?
option_a: All employment he has engaged in
correct_answer: All employment he has engaged in
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(b)(ii), every applicant must state all employment he has engaged in.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: If an applicant has left any employment, what must he state under Rule 020207?
option_a: Why he left the employment
option_b: Only the name of his neighbour
correct_answer: Why he left the employment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(b)(iii), every applicant must state, if he has left any employment, why he did so.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: If an applicant is still in any employment, what must he state under Rule 020207?
option_a: Whether he is under any obligation to remain in it
option_c: Whether he has a new phone number
correct_answer: Whether he is under any obligation to remain in it
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(b)(iv), an applicant still in employment must state whether he is under any obligation to remain in it.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which financial declaration must every applicant make under Rule 020207?
option_a: Whether he is free from financial embarrassment
option_b: Whether he wants a loan immediately
option_c: Whether he owns a private vehicle
correct_answer: Whether he is free from financial embarrassment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020207(b)(v), every applicant for employment by Government must state whether he is free from financial embarrassment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which form must applicants for senior posts complete under Rule 020208?
option_a: Federal Civil Service Commission Application Form FC. 2
option_b: Resumption of Duty Certificate Form L.10
correct_answer: Federal Civil Service Commission Application Form FC. 2
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020208(a), all applicants for senior posts shall complete Federal Civil Service Commission Application Form FC. 2.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: To whom is the FCSC Application Form FC. 2 submitted under Rule 020208?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020208(a), the Federal Civil Service Commission Application Form FC. 2 is submitted to the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: What does the FCSC do after receiving FC. 2 forms under Rule 020208?
option_a: It processes the forms and publishes short-listed names for the prescribed examination
option_c: It sends them only to the Staff Union
option_d: It converts them to leave forms
correct_answer: It processes the forms and publishes short-listed names for the prescribed examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020208(a), the Commission processes the forms and publishes short-listed names for the examination prescribed in Rule 020102.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: For appointment to pensionable establishment, which form accompanies the copy of Form Gen. 69 C?
option_a: Form Gen. 60
correct_answer: Form Gen. 60
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020208(b), for appointment to pensionable establishment, Form Gen. 60 accompanies the copy of Form Gen. 69 C.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which office is among those to receive Form Gen. 60 and Form Gen. 69 C under Rule 020208?
option_a: Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020208(b), the relevant forms are sent to the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, among other listed offices.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which of the following bodies is listed to receive the forms under Rule 020208?
option_a: National Pension Commission
correct_answer: National Pension Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020208(b), the forms are sent to the National Pension Commission, among other listed offices.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: When must a newly appointed Officer enter his personal particulars on Form Gen. 60?
option_a: Immediately after assuming duty
correct_answer: Immediately after assuming duty
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020209, immediately a newly appointed Officer assumes duty, he shall enter his personal particulars on Form Gen. 60.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is Form Gen. 60 called under Rule 020209?
option_a: Staff Records Form
correct_answer: Staff Records Form
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020209, Form Gen. 60 is the Staff Records Form on which a newly appointed Officer enters his personal particulars.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: A copy of Form Gen. 60 is attached to documents forwarded to which body under Rule 020209?
option_a: Pension Fund Administrator or National Pension Commission
correct_answer: Pension Fund Administrator or National Pension Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020209, a copy of Form Gen. 60 is attached to appropriate documents forwarded to the Pension Fund Administrator, National Pension Commission and other relevant Offices or Departments.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who must ensure that all newly employed Officers and Staff sign the Oath of Secrecy on Security?
option_a: Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
correct_answer: Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020210, every Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office must ensure that all newly employed Officers and Staff sign an Oath of Secrecy on Security.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which form is used for the Oath of Secrecy on Security under Rule 020210?
option_a: Form 1
correct_answer: Form 1
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020210, newly employed Officers and Staff sign an Oath of Secrecy on Security using Form 1.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: What must be done with signed Oaths of Secrecy under Rule 020210?
option_a: They must be carefully preserved
option_d: They must be given to private contractors
correct_answer: They must be carefully preserved
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020210, signed Oaths of Secrecy must be carefully preserved.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 020210 is without prejudice to which Act?
option_a: Freedom of Information Act
correct_answer: Freedom of Information Act
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020210, the requirement to sign and preserve the Oath of Secrecy is without prejudice to the provisions of the Freedom of Information Act.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: What does Rule 020211 prohibit?
option_a: Membership of any secret society by a public Officer
option_d: Participation in training by public Officers
correct_answer: Membership of any secret society by a public Officer
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020211, no public Officer shall be a member of any secret society.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: If a person was a member of a secret society before appointment, what must he do under Rule 020211?
option_a: Renounce his membership forthwith by making a statutory declaration
correct_answer: Renounce his membership forthwith by making a statutory declaration
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020211, any public Officer who before appointment was a member of a secret society must renounce membership forthwith by making a statutory declaration.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: How must prior membership of a secret society be renounced under Rule 020211?
option_a: By making a statutory declaration
option_b: By verbal statement to a friend only
correct_answer: By making a statutory declaration
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020211, renunciation of membership of a secret society must be by statutory declaration.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Contravention of Rule 020211 is regarded as what?
option_a: An act of serious misconduct
correct_answer: An act of serious misconduct
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020212, contravention of Rule 020211 on secret society membership is regarded as an act of serious misconduct.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: What disciplinary consequence may follow contravention of Rule 020211 under Rule 020212?
option_a: Appropriate disciplinary action which may include dismissal from the Service
correct_answer: Appropriate disciplinary action which may include dismissal from the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020212, contravention of Rule 020211 attracts appropriate disciplinary action which may include dismissal from the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 2, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 2 of the PSR?
option_a: It covers recruitment, types of appointment, advertising hard-to-fill posts, trainee or pupil appointments, probation, eligibility, prior approval, appointment forms, personal records, oath of secrecy and prohibition of secret society membership
option_b: It deals only with medical treatment abroad
option_c: It deals only with annual leave computation
option_d: It deals only with burial expenses
correct_answer: It covers recruitment, types of appointment, advertising hard-to-fill posts, trainee or pupil appointments, probation, eligibility, prior approval, appointment forms, personal records, oath of secrecy and prohibition of secret society membership
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 2, Rules 020201 to 020212 cover recruitment, types of appointment, difficult-to-fill posts, trainee or pupil appointment, probation, eligibility, prior approval, appointment procedure, personal particulars, oath of secrecy, secret society prohibition and contravention.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Under Rule 020301, how long are Officers on probation required to serve before confirmation in the Service?
option_a: Six months only
correct_answer: Two years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 3, Rule 020301, Officers on probation are required to serve for two years before being confirmed in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Under Rule 020301, the probationary period may be reduced to not less than what period?
option_a: One year
correct_answer: Six months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020301, the probationary period may be reduced, but not to less than six months, by deducting previous satisfactory Public Service in cognate posts involving similar duties.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: What previous service may be deducted from the probationary period under Rule 020301?
option_a: Any private business experience
option_b: Previous Public Service rendered satisfactorily in posts of cognate status involving similar duties
correct_answer: Previous Public Service rendered satisfactorily in posts of cognate status involving similar duties
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020301, previous satisfactory Public Service in posts of cognate status involving similar duties may be deducted when reducing the probationary period.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: The probationary period shall not exceed two years unless an extension is approved by whom?
option_a: The Staff Union
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020301, the probationary period shall not exceed two years unless an extension is approved by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: An extension of probation under Rule 020301 may result in what penalty if the Commission so decides?
option_a: Incremental penalty referred to in Rule 040206
correct_answer: Incremental penalty referred to in Rule 040206
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020301, an extension of probation may result in the incremental penalty referred to in Rule 040206, if the Federal Civil Service Commission so decides.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which statement best describes the general rule on probation under Rule 020301?
option_a: Probation is always one month and cannot be extended
option_b: Probation is two years, may be reduced to not less than six months, and may exceed two years only with FCSC approval
option_c: Probation applies only to retired Officers
correct_answer: Probation is two years, may be reduced to not less than six months, and may exceed two years only with FCSC approval
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020301 provides that probation is normally two years, may be reduced to not less than six months for relevant previous Public Service, and may exceed two years only where the Federal Civil Service Commission approves extension.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Within his probationary period, what is an Officer required to do under Rule 020302?
option_a: Pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment
correct_answer: Pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 3, Rule 020302, an Officer is required within his probationary period to pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: For Officers holding senior posts, the prescribed examinations are those described where?
option_a: Chapter 12 and the Leave Circular
option_b: Chapter 3 and such other examinations as may be specified in the offer of appointment
correct_answer: Chapter 3 and such other examinations as may be specified in the offer of appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020302(a), Officers holding senior posts must pass the examinations described in Chapter 3 and any other examination specified in the individual offer of appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: For clerical grade Officers, what is the prescribed examination under Rule 020302?
option_a: Promotion/Confirmation Examination
correct_answer: Promotion/Confirmation Examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020302(b), the prescribed examination for clerical grade Officers is the Promotion/Confirmation Examination.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: The examinations for technical grades are those prescribed where?
option_a: In the Schemes of Service applicable to the particular post
correct_answer: In the Schemes of Service applicable to the particular post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020302(c), examinations for technical grades are those prescribed in the Schemes of Service applicable to the particular post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020302?
option_a: Every probationary Officer must pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment
option_b: Only Officers on suspension take confirmation examinations
option_c: Confirmation examination is optional for all probationary Officers
option_d: Technical Officers use casual leave rules for confirmation
correct_answer: Every probationary Officer must pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020302 requires an Officer, within his probationary period, to pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: To be eligible for confirmation in Permanent Establishment, what must an Officer appointed on probation do?
option_a: Pass the prescribed examination, if any, and complete probation to the satisfaction of the appointing authority
option_c: Refuse to take the prescribed examination
option_d: Obtain approval from a Staff Union only
correct_answer: Pass the prescribed examination, if any, and complete probation to the satisfaction of the appointing authority
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020303, an Officer on probation must pass the prescribed examination, if any, and complete the probationary period to the satisfaction of the authority empowered to appoint him.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Who must be satisfied before a probationary Officer is confirmed under Rule 020303?
option_a: The authority empowered to appoint him
correct_answer: The authority empowered to appoint him
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020303, the Officer must complete the probationary period to the satisfaction of the authority empowered to appoint him.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: At the end of the probationary period, what happens to the Officer unless his appointment is terminated or extended?
option_a: He is confirmed in his appointment
correct_answer: He is confirmed in his appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020303, at the end of the probationary period, the Officer will be confirmed in his appointment unless his probationary appointment is terminated or extended.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which of the following may happen at the end of probation under Rule 020303?
option_a: Confirmation, termination or extension of probation
correct_answer: Confirmation, termination or extension of probation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020303, at the end of probation, the Officer is confirmed unless his probationary appointment is terminated or extended.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Under Rule 020304, how are recommendations on confirmation of Officers holding senior posts made?
option_a: In the progress report prescribed in Chapter 5 of the Rules
correct_answer: In the progress report prescribed in Chapter 5 of the Rules
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020304, recommendations of Permanent Secretaries/Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices regarding confirmation of Officers holding senior posts shall be made in the progress report prescribed in Chapter 5 of the Rules.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Who makes recommendations regarding confirmation of Officers holding senior posts under Rule 020304?
option_a: Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
correct_answer: Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020304, Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices make recommendations regarding confirmation of Officers holding senior posts.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Rule 020304 links senior post confirmation recommendation to which chapter?
option_a: Chapter 5
correct_answer: Chapter 5
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020304, recommendations for confirmation of Officers holding senior posts are made in the progress report prescribed in Chapter 5.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Under Rule 020305, membership of the Junior Staff Committee and Senior Staff Committee in Parastatals shall include whose representative?
option_a: Representative of the Department of Human Resource Management of the supervising Ministry
option_c: Representative of a private travel agency
correct_answer: Representative of the Department of Human Resource Management of the supervising Ministry
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020305, membership of JSC and SSC in Parastatals shall include the representative of the Department of Human Resource Management of the supervising Ministry.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which office must have an observer in the JSC and SSC in Parastatals under Rule 020305?
option_a: Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020305, membership of the Junior Staff Committee and Senior Staff Committee in Parastatals shall include an observer from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Rule 020305 concerns membership of which committees in Parastatals?
option_a: Junior Staff Committee and Senior Staff Committee
correct_answer: Junior Staff Committee and Senior Staff Committee
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020305 provides for membership of the Junior Staff Committee and Senior Staff Committee in Parastatals.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which statement correctly summarises Rule 020305?
option_a: JSC and SSC in Parastatals must include HRM representative of the supervising Ministry and an OHCSF observer
option_b: JSC and SSC in Parastatals consist only of private consultants
option_c: JSC and SSC in Parastatals are abolished
option_d: JSC and SSC in Parastatals are controlled only by Staff Union officials
correct_answer: JSC and SSC in Parastatals must include HRM representative of the supervising Ministry and an OHCSF observer
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020305, the Junior Staff Committee and Senior Staff Committee in Parastatals include the supervising Ministry’s HRM representative and an observer from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Under Rule 020306, a newly recruited Officer may sit for compulsory examinations for confirmation after spending what minimum period?
option_a: Six months and above
correct_answer: Six months and above
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020306, a newly recruited Officer who has spent six months and above shall be allowed to sit for compulsory examinations for confirmation in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Rule 020306 is without prejudice to which rule?
option_a: Rule 020301
correct_answer: Rule 020301
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020306, the provision allowing newly recruited Officers who have spent six months and above to sit for compulsory examinations is without prejudice to Rule 020301.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: What type of examinations may a newly recruited Officer sit for after six months and above under Rule 020306?
option_a: Compulsory examinations for confirmation in the Service
correct_answer: Compulsory examinations for confirmation in the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020306, a newly recruited Officer who has spent six months and above shall be allowed to sit for compulsory examinations for confirmation in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Under Rule 020307, transfer from one senior post to another within the Federal Public Service requires whose prior approval?
option_a: Federal Civil Service Commission or appropriate board of relevant agency
correct_answer: Federal Civil Service Commission or appropriate board of relevant agency
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, transfer from one senior post to another or from one class to another within the Federal Public Service requires prior approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission or the appropriate board of the relevant agency.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Before seeking transfer to another post under Rule 020307, an Officer must have served how long in his original post?
option_a: Minimum period of six months
correct_answer: Minimum period of six months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, an Officer must have served for a minimum period of six months in his original post before seeking transfer to another post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: To whom must an application for transfer under Rule 020307 be submitted?
option_a: Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office or Agency of the applicant
correct_answer: Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office or Agency of the applicant
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, an application for transfer must be submitted to the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office or Agency of the applicant.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: What must an Officer’s transfer application state under Rule 020307?
option_a: The applicant’s reasons for desiring transfer and his qualifications for the work to be undertaken
correct_answer: The applicant’s reasons for desiring transfer and his qualifications for the work to be undertaken
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, the transfer application must state the applicant’s reasons for desiring a transfer and his qualifications for the work to be undertaken.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Who forwards the transfer application to the Federal Civil Service Commission under Rule 020307?
option_a: The Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
correct_answer: The Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office forwards the transfer application to the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which statement must accompany the transfer application under Rule 020307?
option_a: A statement on how the applicant has performed his duties
option_b: A statement on the Officer’s family ceremonies only
option_c: A statement on the Officer’s private business only
option_d: A statement from the Officer’s neighbour
correct_answer: A statement on how the applicant has performed his duties
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, the application should be forwarded with a statement showing how the applicant has performed his duties.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: The statement forwarded with a transfer application must also indicate what under Rule 020307?
option_a: Whether the applicant is considered well qualified for the post desired
option_b: Whether the applicant owns a private vehicle
option_c: Whether the applicant prefers annual leave abroad
option_d: Whether the applicant belongs to a social club
correct_answer: Whether the applicant is considered well qualified for the post desired
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, the forwarded statement must indicate whether the applicant is considered well qualified for the post desired.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: The Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office must include what recommendation on the transfer application?
option_a: Recommendation as to the grant or refusal of the application
correct_answer: Recommendation as to the grant or refusal of the application
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020307, the forwarded statement must include recommendations as to the grant or refusal of the transfer application.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 3.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 3 of the PSR?
option_a: It covers probation period, compulsory examination, confirmation or termination, progress reports for senior posts, JSC/SSC membership, COMPRO examination eligibility and transfer within the Federal Public Service
option_b: It deals only with medical treatment abroad
option_c: It deals only with burial expenses
option_d: It deals only with annual leave
correct_answer: It covers probation period, compulsory examination, confirmation or termination, progress reports for senior posts, JSC/SSC membership, COMPRO examination eligibility and transfer within the Federal Public Service
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 3, Rules 020301 to 020307 cover rules for appointment on probation, including probation period, compulsory examination, confirmation or termination, senior post confirmation reports, JSC/SSC membership in Parastatals, COMPRO examination eligibility and transfer within the Federal Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020401, why may short-term appointments be made in the Public Service?
option_a: To punish Officers for poor performance
option_b: To fill observed skills gaps or shore up the capacities of existing Officers
option_c: To replace all pensionable appointments permanently
option_d: To avoid using the Schemes of Service
correct_answer: To fill observed skills gaps or shore up the capacities of existing Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 4, Rule 020401, short-term appointments may be made where specialized or new/emerging skills are required to fill observed gaps or strengthen the capacities of existing Officers.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which of the following is one category of short-term appointment listed under Rule 020401?
option_a: Contract Appointment
correct_answer: Contract Appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020401, Contract Appointment is one of the categories of short-term appointments in the Federal Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which option correctly lists categories of short-term appointment under Rule 020401?
option_a: Contract Appointment, Sabbatical Appointment, Career Exchange Programme, Talent Sourcing Strategy, Internship and Volunteerism
option_c: Annual Leave, Casual Leave, Sick Leave and Maternity Leave
correct_answer: Contract Appointment, Sabbatical Appointment, Career Exchange Programme, Talent Sourcing Strategy, Internship and Volunteerism
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020401 lists Contract Appointment, Sabbatical Appointment, Career Exchange Programme, Talent Sourcing Strategy, Internship and Volunteerism as categories of short-term appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Short-term appointments under Rule 020401 may involve specialized skills that are what?
option_a: Only political skills
option_b: Only skills prescribed in disciplinary rules
option_c: Prescribed or not prescribed in the Schemes of Service
option_d: Only skills used by retired Officers
correct_answer: Prescribed or not prescribed in the Schemes of Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020401, specialized or new/emerging skills may or may not have been prescribed in the Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is a Contract Appointment under Rule 020402?
option_a: A permanent pensionable appointment
option_b: A temporary appointment that does not provide for payment of pension
option_c: An automatic promotion into a senior post
option_d: A leave arrangement for study abroad
correct_answer: A temporary appointment that does not provide for payment of pension
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020402, a Contract Appointment is a temporary appointment that does not provide for payment of pension and is made for a specific period.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who makes contract appointment to posts under Rule 020402 in the core Federal Civil Service?
option_a: The Staff Union
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020402, contract appointment to the relevant level is made by the Federal Civil Service Commission in the core Federal Civil Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who makes contract appointment in Parastatals and Agencies under Rule 020402?
option_a: The Governing Board
option_c: The Federal Road Safety Corps only
correct_answer: The Governing Board
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020402, in the case of Parastatals and Agencies, contract appointment is made by the Governing Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: How must a contract appointment be recorded under Rule 020402?
option_a: By verbal promise only
option_b: In a formal document of agreement
correct_answer: In a formal document of agreement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020402, a contract appointment must be recorded in a formal document of agreement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Contract Appointment may be offered where the Service no longer has what?
option_a: Officers with specific skills needed to perform related functions
correct_answer: Officers with specific skills needed to perform related functions
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(i), Contract Appointment may be offered if it is established that the Service no longer has Officers with specific skills provided in the approved Schemes of Service to perform the related functions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020403, contract appointment may arise from which situation?
option_a: Emerging cadres, courses, skills and the creation of new ones
option_b: An Officer’s refusal to resume from leave
correct_answer: Emerging cadres, courses, skills and the creation of new ones
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(ii), Contract Appointment may be based on circumstances arising from emerging cadres, courses, skills and the creation of new ones as well as prevailing realities.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Contract Appointment may be tied to what under Rule 020403?
option_a: Funded projects or programmes with specified life span
correct_answer: Funded projects or programmes with specified life span
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(iii), Contract Appointment may be tied to funded projects or programmes with specified life span.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: When may Contract Appointment be offered to expatriates under Rule 020403?
option_a: Only when suitable Nigerians are not available
option_c: Only when a post is below GL. 06
option_d: Only after all Nigerians are retired
correct_answer: Only when suitable Nigerians are not available
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(iv), Contract Appointment may be offered to expatriates only when suitable Nigerians are not available.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which Nigerian may be considered for Contract Appointment under Rule 020403?
option_a: A pensioner
option_b: A newly recruited Officer on probation only
correct_answer: A pensioner
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(v)(a), Contract Appointment may be offered to Nigerians if they are pensioners.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020403, a Nigerian may be considered for Contract Appointment if he is at least what age at the time of appointment?
option_a: 35 years
correct_answer: 50 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(v)(b), Contract Appointment may be offered to Nigerians if they are 50 years of age or over at the time they are being appointed.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Where a Nigerian specifically requests employment on contract terms, what further condition applies under Rule 020403?
option_a: It must be deemed in the best interest of the Service
option_b: It must be approved by the Staff Union only
option_c: It must be for annual leave purposes
correct_answer: It must be deemed in the best interest of the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(v)(c), a Nigerian who specifically requests contract terms may be employed if it is deemed in the best interest of the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Where specialized competencies or skills are required for Contract Appointment, how must the post be advertised under Rule 020403?
option_a: In at least three national newspapers
option_d: Only through a private WhatsApp group
correct_answer: In at least three national newspapers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020403(v)(d), where the candidate possesses specialized competencies or skills, such posts must be duly advertised in at least three national newspapers.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020404, the conditions of service of an Officer on short-term appointment are those provided where?
option_a: In his contract
option_c: In the Staff Union constitution only
correct_answer: In his contract
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020404(i), the conditions of service of an Officer on short-term appointment are those provided in his contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Do PSR privileges, emoluments or allowances automatically apply to an Officer on short-term appointment?
option_a: Yes, they apply automatically in every case
option_b: No, unless they are stated in the contract itself
option_c: Yes, if the Officer is above 50 years
option_d: Yes, if the Officer requests them
correct_answer: No, unless they are stated in the contract itself
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020404(i), the privileges, emoluments or allowances in the PSR do not apply to a short-term appointee unless stated in the contract itself.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Questions on interpretation of a short-term appointment contract affecting conditions of service should be referred to whom?
option_a: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020404(i), questions on interpretation of a contract affecting conditions of service should be referred to the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020404, what is the position of spouses married to Nigerians before Nigerian citizenship is granted?
option_a: They should remain on contract until granted Nigerian citizenship before being considered for permanent appointment
option_b: They must immediately become permanent Officers
option_c: They are automatically placed on pensionable appointment
option_d: They must be exempted from contract rules
correct_answer: They should remain on contract until granted Nigerian citizenship before being considered for permanent appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020404(iii), spouses married to Nigerians should remain on contract until granted Nigerian citizenship before being considered for permanent appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020405, which body in an MDA identifies required skills for Contract Appointment?
option_a: The Senior Staff Committee
correct_answer: The Senior Staff Committee
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(i), MDAs through their Senior Staff Committee identify required skills and defend the skills at the OHCSF.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the role of the OHCSF in the skill-identification process under Rule 020405?
option_a: To work out and approve waiver for the desired skills
option_d: To replace the Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: To work out and approve waiver for the desired skills
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(i), the OHCSF works out and approves waiver for the desired skills after the MDA defends the identified skills.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which form must a prospective applicant submit for Contract Appointment under Rule 020405?
option_a: FCSC Form 2
correct_answer: FCSC Form 2
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(ii), the prospective applicant must apply by submitting a duly filled FCSC Form 2 as required.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020405, Contract Appointment must not be made below which salary grade level?
option_a: SGL. 06
correct_answer: SGL. 12
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(iii), the post to which contract appointment is made must not be below SGL. 12.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Contract Appointment must be based on what process under Rule 020405?
option_a: Fair, open and competitive selection process
correct_answer: Fair, open and competitive selection process
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(iv), Contract Appointment must be based on merit through a fair, open and competitive selection process.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Contract Appointment under Rule 020405 must not jeopardize what?
