option_a: The career prospects of serving Officers
correct_answer: The career prospects of serving Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(iv), Contract Appointment must not jeopardize the career prospects of serving Officers.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: For Contract Appointment of non-Nigerians, who undertakes immigration responsibilities under Rule 020405?
option_a: Government
correct_answer: Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(v), Government undertakes immigration responsibilities, including relevant working or residence permit, for non-Nigerians.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the normal duration of Contract Appointment under Rule 020405?
option_a: One or two years, renewable but not more than four years in all
correct_answer: One or two years, renewable but not more than four years in all
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020405(vii), the duration of Contract Appointment should be one or two years and renewable, but not more than four years in all.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020406, a Contract Officer must be responsible for what as part of his duties?
option_a: Mentoring serving Officers
correct_answer: Mentoring serving Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020406(i), a Contract Officer must, as part of his duties, be responsible for mentoring serving Officers as a condition for the contract appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: What undertaking must a Contract Officer sign under Rule 020406?
option_a: To accept posting or transfer to any part of the country
correct_answer: To accept posting or transfer to any part of the country
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020406(ii), a Contract Officer must sign an undertaking to accept posting or transfer to any part of the country.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: How are Officers appointed on contract appraised under Rule 020406?
option_a: Through confidential report as applicable in the Service
correct_answer: Through confidential report as applicable in the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020406(iii), Officers appointed on contract are subject to performance appraisal through confidential report as applicable in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020406, Contract staff must sign the oath of secrecy in line with which rule?
option_a: Rule 020210
correct_answer: Rule 020210
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020406(iv), Contract staff must sign the oath of secrecy in line with PSR Rule 020210.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who may terminate a Contract Appointment in accordance with the terms of the contract?
option_a: Government
correct_answer: Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020407(a), an appointment on contract may be terminated by Government at any time in accordance with the terms specified in the contract itself.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: A recommendation to terminate the appointment of a Contract Officer must be accompanied by what?
option_a: A full statement of the consideration which prompted it
correct_answer: A full statement of the consideration which prompted it
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020407(a), a recommendation to the Federal Civil Service Commission for termination must be accompanied by a full statement of the consideration which prompted it.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: On receiving a termination recommendation, what may the Federal Civil Service Commission decide?
option_a: Whether to terminate forthwith or allow the Officer to submit formal representation
option_b: Whether to grant annual leave only
option_d: Whether to appoint the Officer permanently without review
correct_answer: Whether to terminate forthwith or allow the Officer to submit formal representation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020407(a), the FCSC decides whether the appointment should be terminated forthwith or whether the Officer should be offered opportunity to submit formal representation before final decision.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Termination of Contract Appointment by the holder is subject to what?
option_a: The terms of the contract
correct_answer: The terms of the contract
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020407(b), termination of a contract appointment by the holder is subject to the terms of the contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: Questions about waiving penalty under a contract agreement should be referred to whom?
option_a: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020407(b), any question concerning waiver of penalty under a contract agreement shall be referred to the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: An Officer on contract who desires re-engagement must notify Government how?
option_a: In writing through the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
option_b: By verbal message to a colleague
option_d: By refusing to proceed on leave
correct_answer: In writing through the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020408, an Officer serving on contract who desires re-engagement must inform Government in writing through the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: How long before leave is due must a Contract Officer request re-engagement?
option_a: Not less than four months
correct_answer: Not less than four months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020408, the Officer must give written notification not less than four months before his leave is due.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 1 of 2.
question: If a Contract Officer gives no notification of desire for re-engagement, what may be assumed?
option_a: That he does not desire re-engagement
option_d: That he is on study leave
correct_answer: That he does not desire re-engagement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020408, in the absence of notification, it may be assumed that the Contract Officer does not desire re-engagement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: After receiving a Contract Officer’s request for re-engagement, whose consent must the Permanent Secretary or Head obtain before forwarding recommendation to the FCSC?
option_a: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020409, the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office must obtain the consent of the OHCSF before forwarding recommendation for re-engagement to the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What report must accompany the re-engagement recommendation unless recently forwarded?
option_a: An up-to-date confidential report on the Officer
correct_answer: An up-to-date confidential report on the Officer
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020409, an up-to-date confidential report on the Officer must be enclosed unless such report has been forwarded within the previous two months.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What may the Permanent Secretary receive in reply under Rule 020409?
option_a: Authority to inform the Officer that arrangements will be made to offer re-engagement
option_b: Authority to dismiss all contract staff automatically
option_c: A leave roster for the next year
correct_answer: Authority to inform the Officer that arrangements will be made to offer re-engagement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020409(a), the Permanent Secretary or Head may receive authority to inform the Officer that arrangements will be made to offer re-engagement during leave and the proposed terms.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Where the original and duplicate re-engagement contract are received, what should the Permanent Secretary or Head do?
option_a: Obtain the Officer’s witnessed signature on both copies, deliver the duplicate to the Officer and return the original to OHCSF
option_d: Send both copies to the Staff Union
correct_answer: Obtain the Officer’s witnessed signature on both copies, deliver the duplicate to the Officer and return the original to OHCSF
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020409(b), the Permanent Secretary or Head obtains the Officer’s witnessed signature on both copies, delivers the duplicate to the Officer and returns the original to the OHCSF.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: If a Permanent Secretary cannot recommend re-engagement of a Contract Officer, whose approval must be sought before informing the Officer?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020410, where the Permanent Secretary or Head cannot recommend re-engagement, approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission must be sought before informing the Officer.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: After approval is received not to re-engage a Contract Officer, what must the Permanent Secretary do?
option_a: Inform the Officer without delay
option_c: Publish the matter in newspapers first
correct_answer: Inform the Officer without delay
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020410, after receiving approval, the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office must inform the Officer without delay that he will not be re-engaged.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: When will service under a new contract be treated as continuous?
option_a: Where re-engagement is completed by signing a new contract before the end of vacation leave under the expiring contract
option_b: Where the Officer signs after five years
option_c: Where the Officer gives no notice
option_d: Where the Officer refuses to sign
correct_answer: Where re-engagement is completed by signing a new contract before the end of vacation leave under the expiring contract
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020411, service under a new contract is treated as continuous if re-engagement is completed by signing a new contract before the end of vacation leave granted under the expiring contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Where retired Officers are re-engaged into career posts, on what grade level are they appointed?
option_a: The grade level immediately below that on which they retired
option_b: The same grade level plus two levels
option_c: Any grade level chosen by the Officer
correct_answer: The grade level immediately below that on which they retired
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020412, retired Officers re-engaged into career posts are appointed on the grade level immediately below that on which they retired.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Retired Officers re-engaged into career posts may maintain what under Rule 020412?
option_a: Their last step at retirement
correct_answer: Their last step at retirement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020412, retired Officers re-engaged into career posts are eligible to maintain their last step at retirement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: How is the remuneration of non-Public or non-Civil Servants determined under Rule 020412?
option_a: Based on negotiable terms by the parties concerned
correct_answer: Based on negotiable terms by the parties concerned
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020412, the remuneration of non-Public or non-Civil Servants is based on negotiable terms by the parties concerned.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is Sabbatical Appointment under Rule 020413?
option_a: Appointment of an Officer on GL. 15 or equivalent and above for research and professional development
option_b: Appointment of junior staff on GL. 03 only
correct_answer: Appointment of an Officer on GL. 15 or equivalent and above for research and professional development
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020413, Sabbatical Appointment applies to an Officer on GL. 15 or equivalent and above for research and professional development.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is the duration of Sabbatical Appointment under Rule 020413?
option_a: 12 calendar months
correct_answer: 12 calendar months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020413, Sabbatical Appointment shall be for a period of 12 calendar months.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020414, who pays travel expenses, lodging and sundries during Sabbatical Appointment?
option_a: The host MDA or Organization
correct_answer: The host MDA or Organization
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020414, the host MDA or Organization is responsible for payment of travel expenses, lodging and sundries.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020414, who continues to pay the Officer’s salary during Sabbatical Appointment?
option_a: The parent MDA or Organization
correct_answer: The parent MDA or Organization
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020414, the parent MDA or Organization continues to pay the Officer’s salary for the duration of the leave.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What does Internship connote under Rule 020415?
option_a: A structured experience related to a student’s or graduate’s discipline or career goal
option_c: A permanent appointment on pensionable terms
correct_answer: A structured experience related to a student’s or graduate’s discipline or career goal
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020415, Internship connotes a structured experience related to a student’s or graduate’s discipline or career goal.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is one purpose of Internship under Rule 020415?
option_a: To facilitate acquisition of practical skills, workplace experience and greater professional knowledge
correct_answer: To facilitate acquisition of practical skills, workplace experience and greater professional knowledge
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020415, Internship facilitates acquisition of practical skills, workplace experience and greater knowledge of the profession.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What does Volunteerism mean under Rule 020416?
option_a: Offering one’s time or talents for charitable, educational or other worthwhile activities
correct_answer: Offering one’s time or talents for charitable, educational or other worthwhile activities
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020416, Volunteerism denotes offering one’s time or talents for charitable, educational or other worthwhile activities, especially in one’s community.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: According to Rule 020416, volunteers are driven by what?
option_a: Passion to leave a noble legacy of service to humanity
correct_answer: Passion to leave a noble legacy of service to humanity
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020416, volunteers are driven by passion to leave a noble legacy of service to humanity.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Where is the Focal Office for volunteer programme established under Rule 020417?
option_a: In the OHCSF
option_d: In the Pension Fund Administrator office
correct_answer: In the OHCSF
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(i), a Focal Office shall be established in the OHCSF to identify fields or tasks available for volunteer programmes and disseminate information.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What are MDAs required to establish in supportive role for internship and volunteerism under Rule 020417?
option_a: Desks for the two programmes
correct_answer: Desks for the two programmes
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(i), MDAs in supportive role are required to establish Desks for the two programmes.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What must the Focal Office upload on the OHCSF website under Rule 020417?
option_a: Skills, benefits, conditions of engagement and requisite qualifications
correct_answer: Skills, benefits, conditions of engagement and requisite qualifications
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(ii), the Focal Office uploads skills highlighting benefits and conditions of engagement with requisite qualifications on the OHCSF website.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: How do prospective volunteers apply under Rule 020417?
option_a: In response to advertisement on the OHCSF website
correct_answer: In response to advertisement on the OHCSF website
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(iii), prospective volunteers with specialty in preferred fields apply for engagement in response to advertisement on the OHCSF website.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Before engagement, prospective volunteers must obtain which two clearances or certifications?
option_a: Medical fitness by recognized HCP and security clearance from the Police
option_b: Approval from a private school and family consent
option_c: Annual leave approval and pension clearance
correct_answer: Medical fitness by recognized HCP and security clearance from the Police
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(iv), prospective volunteers must be certified medically fit by a recognized Healthcare Provider and obtain security clearance from the Police before engagement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What must interns engaged directly by MDAs submit under Rule 020417?
option_a: Reference letter from their respective institutions
correct_answer: Reference letter from their respective institutions
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(v), interns to be engaged directly by MDAs shall submit reference letters from their respective institutions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: At the end of internship or volunteer programmes, what should successful candidates receive?
option_a: Letters of commendation
correct_answer: Letters of commendation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(vii), successful candidates shall be given letters of commendation at the end of the programmes.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: For how long may interns be engaged part-time during an academic session?
option_a: 3 to 6 months
correct_answer: 3 to 6 months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020418, interns shall be engaged for 3 to 6 months on part-time during an academic session.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is the maximum full-time internship period under Rule 020418?
option_a: Not more than 12 months
correct_answer: Not more than 12 months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020418, interns may be engaged full-time for a period of not more than 12 months.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: For how long may volunteers be engaged at a time under Rule 020418?
option_a: Maximum of 12 months
correct_answer: Maximum of 12 months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020418, volunteers shall be engaged for a maximum of 12 months at a time.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Stipends for Volunteers shall be in accordance with what under Rule 020419?
option_a: The rate contained in the National Volunteering Policy by the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation
correct_answer: The rate contained in the National Volunteering Policy by the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020419, stipends for Volunteers shall be in accordance with the rate contained in the National Volunteering Policy by the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who is responsible for payment of stipends to Volunteers during their service?
option_a: Host MDAs
correct_answer: Host MDAs
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020419, Host MDAs are responsible for payment of stipends to Volunteers during the period of their service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Stipends paid to interns are at what rate under Rule 020417?
option_a: Rates prescribed by relevant circulars issued from time to time
option_b: Rates fixed by the intern personally
option_d: Rates determined by the Staff Union
correct_answer: Rates prescribed by relevant circulars issued from time to time
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020417(vi), stipends paid to interns shall be at the rates prescribed by relevant circulars issued from time to time.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who may qualify as interns under Rule 020420?
option_a: Postgraduates, undergraduates or students in other tertiary institutions
correct_answer: Postgraduates, undergraduates or students in other tertiary institutions
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020420, interns must be postgraduates, undergraduates or students in other tertiary institutions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which qualification is listed for volunteers under Rule 020420?
option_a: University Degree, HND, NCE, ND, SSCE or its equivalent
correct_answer: University Degree, HND, NCE, ND, SSCE or its equivalent
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020420, volunteers must possess a University Degree, HND, NCE, ND, SSCE or its equivalent.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020421, which departments or units must be represented in discussions on short-term engagement contracts?
option_a: Human Resources, Finance and Accounts, User Department or Unit, and Legal Unit
correct_answer: Human Resources, Finance and Accounts, User Department or Unit, and Legal Unit
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020421(a), Human Resources Management, Finance and Accounts Department, User Department or Unit and Legal Unit must be represented in discussions on short-term engagement contracts.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: At what level must representation be made in the contract-discussion process under Rule 020421?
option_a: Director level
correct_answer: Director level
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020421(a)(v), representation in the negotiation, drafting and execution of short-term engagement contracts shall be at the level of Director.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: After negotiations for short-term engagement, what document must be issued to the employee?
option_a: A letter of appointment
correct_answer: A letter of appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020421(b), after negotiations, a letter of appointment shall be issued to the employee.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: The letter of appointment after short-term engagement negotiations must be endorsed by whom?
option_a: The Permanent Secretary or Chief Executive
correct_answer: The Permanent Secretary or Chief Executive
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020421(b), the letter of appointment shall be duly endorsed by the Permanent Secretary or Chief Executive.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: What must the letter of appointment indicate under Rule 020421?
option_a: The terms of the contract of engagement by the parties
correct_answer: The terms of the contract of engagement by the parties
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020421(b), the letter of appointment must indicate the terms of the contract of engagement by the parties.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Where is the template of short-term engagement stated to be found?
option_a: Appendix C
correct_answer: Appendix C
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020421, the template of short-term engagement is stated to be in Appendix C.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 4, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 4 of the PSR?
option_a: It regulates short-term engagements including contract appointment, sabbatical appointment, internship, volunteerism, re-engagement, remuneration, tenure, qualifications and legal framework
option_b: It deals only with annual leave
option_c: It deals only with disciplinary dismissal
option_d: It deals only with burial expenses
correct_answer: It regulates short-term engagements including contract appointment, sabbatical appointment, internship, volunteerism, re-engagement, remuneration, tenure, qualifications and legal framework
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 4, Rules 020401 to 020421 cover short-term engagements, including Contract Appointment, Sabbatical Appointment, Internship, Volunteerism, re-engagement, remuneration, tenure, qualifications and the legal framework for processing short-term engagements.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Under Rule 020501, what is transfer?
option_a: The temporary release of an Officer for training only
option_b: The permanent release of an Officer from one scheduled Service to another or from one class to another within the same Service
option_c: The posting of an Officer within the same unit for one week
option_d: The suspension of an Officer from duty
correct_answer: The permanent release of an Officer from one scheduled Service to another or from one class to another within the same Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 5, Rule 020501(a), transfer is the permanent release of an Officer from one scheduled Service to another or from one class to another within the same Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Under Rule 020501, what is secondment?
option_a: A permanent release from one Service to another
option_b: The temporary release of an Officer to another Government approved body or recognized International Organization or body for a specified period
option_c: An automatic promotion to a higher grade
correct_answer: The temporary release of an Officer to another Government approved body or recognized International Organization or body for a specified period
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020501(b), secondment means the temporary release of an Officer to the service of another Government approved body or any recognized International Organization or body for a specified period.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which statement correctly distinguishes transfer from secondment?
option_a: Transfer is permanent, while secondment is temporary
option_b: Transfer is always disciplinary, while secondment is always promotion
option_c: Transfer applies only to retired Officers, while secondment applies only to trainees
option_d: Transfer and secondment mean exactly the same thing
correct_answer: Transfer is permanent, while secondment is temporary
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020501 defines transfer as permanent release, while secondment is temporary release for a specified period.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Secondment may be to which of the following?
option_a: Another Government approved body or recognized International Organization
option_c: Only a private club without recognition
correct_answer: Another Government approved body or recognized International Organization
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020501(b), secondment may be to another Government approved body or any recognized International Organization or body.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Who considers applications for transfer or secondment to posts graded GL. 06 and below?
option_a: The appropriate Committee of the benefiting Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office
option_b: The Federal Ministry of Health only
correct_answer: The appropriate Committee of the benefiting Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020502(i), applications for transfer or secondment to posts graded GL. 06 and below are considered by the appropriate Committee of the benefiting Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Who approves transfer or secondment to posts graded GL. 06 and below?
option_a: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
correct_answer: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020502(i), transfer or secondment to posts graded GL. 06 and below is approved by the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Who determines applications for transfer or secondment to posts graded GL. 07–10 in any Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020502(ii), applications for transfer or secondment to posts graded GL. 07–10 in any Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Office are determined by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Officers seeking transfer from scheduled establishments on Salary GL. 07–10 are required to do what?
option_a: Sit for the Annual Competitive Civil Service Entry Examination
option_d: Apply only through the Staff Union
correct_answer: Sit for the Annual Competitive Civil Service Entry Examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020502(ii), Officers seeking transfer from scheduled establishments on Salary GL. 07–10 are required to sit for the Annual Competitive Civil Service Entry Examination.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which statement best reflects the authority to process transfer or secondment under Rule 020502?
option_a: GL. 06 and below are handled by the benefiting Ministry’s appropriate Committee and approved by the Permanent Secretary or Head; GL. 07–10 are determined by the FCSC
option_b: All transfers are approved by the Officer’s supervisor alone
option_c: All secondments are approved by the Staff Union
option_d: Only the receiving Officer decides the matter
correct_answer: GL. 06 and below are handled by the benefiting Ministry’s appropriate Committee and approved by the Permanent Secretary or Head; GL. 07–10 are determined by the FCSC
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020502 provides separate processing authorities: GL. 06 and below by the appropriate Committee and Permanent Secretary or Head, while GL. 07–10 are determined by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: What confidential reports must be furnished when processing transfer or secondment?
option_a: Reports covering the last three years, or the whole service if less than three years
correct_answer: Reports covering the last three years, or the whole service if less than three years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(a), confidential reports covering the last three years, or the whole service if less than three years, must be furnished.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: How is an Officer on transfer from State to Federal Service placed?
option_a: On a grade level lower than his current grade level
option_b: On the same grade level automatically
option_c: On a grade level higher than his current grade level
option_d: On any level chosen by the Officer
correct_answer: On a grade level lower than his current grade level
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(b), an Officer on transfer from State to Federal Service shall be placed on a grade level lower than his current grade level.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Transfer to the Federal Service is limited to which posts?
option_a: Posts graded GL. 07 to 14 or equivalent
correct_answer: Posts graded GL. 07 to 14 or equivalent
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(c), transfer to the Federal Service is limited to posts graded GL. 07 to 14 or its equivalent.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Under Rule 020503, an Officer on transfer or secondment must have what employment status?
option_a: He must have been confirmed
option_b: He must still be on probation
correct_answer: He must have been confirmed
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(d), an Officer on transfer or secondment must have been confirmed.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Besides confirmation, what must align with the Schemes of Service for an Officer on transfer or secondment?
option_a: His qualifications, experience and career progression
correct_answer: His qualifications, experience and career progression
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(d), the Officer’s qualifications, experience and career progression must be in accordance with the Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: What evidence is required from both releasing and accepting agencies for transfer or secondment?
option_a: Evidence of concurrence
correct_answer: Evidence of concurrence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(e), there must be evidence of concurrence to the transfer or secondment by the releasing and accepting agencies.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: What is the maximum first-instance period of secondment to another Government, approved body or recognized International Organization?
option_a: Two years
correct_answer: Two years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(f), secondment shall be for a maximum period of two years in the first instance.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: After the first-instance period of secondment, what may the Officer do?
option_a: Apply for extension or return to his former post
option_d: Convert the secondment to annual leave
correct_answer: Apply for extension or return to his former post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(f), after the first-instance secondment period, the Officer may apply for extension or return to his former post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Who must approve extensions of secondment under Rule 020503?
option_a: The appropriate Committees and the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board
correct_answer: The appropriate Committees and the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(f), all extensions of secondment must be approved by the appropriate Committees and the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: What is the total maximum period of ordinary secondment under Rule 020503(f)?
option_a: Four years
correct_answer: Four years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(f), the total period of such secondment must not exceed four years.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: If secondment is in the public interest, what is the maximum period allowed?
option_a: Six years
correct_answer: Six years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(g), where it is in the public interest to second an Officer, the period of secondment shall not exceed six years.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: During secondment, what happens to the Officer’s substantive post?
option_a: He continues to hold his substantive post
option_b: He automatically loses his substantive post
option_c: He is treated as dismissed from his post
option_d: His post is converted to casual appointment
correct_answer: He continues to hold his substantive post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(h), during the period of secondment the Officer continues to hold his substantive post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: During secondment, the Officer is entitled to what career benefits?
option_a: Increment and promotion
correct_answer: Increment and promotion
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(h), during the period of secondment the Officer is entitled to increment and promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: How is an Officer on secondment treated under Rule 020503?
option_a: As having been posted on special duty
correct_answer: As having been posted on special duty
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020503(h), an Officer on secondment is treated as having been posted on special duty.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: During ordinary secondment, who is responsible for the Officer’s emoluments?
option_a: The benefiting organization
correct_answer: The benefiting organization
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020504, during secondment the benefiting organization is responsible for the Officer’s emoluments.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Where an Officer is released on secondment in public interest and there is a differential in pay between releasing and receiving MDAs, who pays the salary?
option_a: The MDA with the higher pay
correct_answer: The MDA with the higher pay
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020504, where secondment is in the public interest and there is a differential in payments, the MDA with the higher pay is responsible for payment of salary.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Under Rule 020504, who pays non-salary allowances during secondment?
option_a: The receiving MDA
option_b: The releasing MDA in every case
correct_answer: The receiving MDA
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020504, notwithstanding the salary arrangement, all non-salary allowances shall be paid by the receiving MDA.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: The emoluments and incremental date of an Officer on transfer are governed by which rule?
option_a: Rule 040103
correct_answer: Rule 040103
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020505, the emoluments and incremental date of an Officer on transfer are governed by Rule 040103.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Rule 020505 deals mainly with what subject?
option_a: Salary on transfer
correct_answer: Salary on transfer
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020505 is titled salary on transfer and provides that the emoluments and incremental date of an Officer on transfer are governed by Rule 040103.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: When may an applicant be considered for transfer-on-promotion to any MDA?
option_a: Only in response to an advertised post
correct_answer: Only in response to an advertised post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020506, no applicant shall be considered for transfer-on-promotion to any MDA except in response to an advertised post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which statement is correct about transfer-on-promotion under Rule 020506?
option_a: It must be in response to an advertised post
option_b: It is automatic for all Officers
option_d: It is handled only through verbal instruction
correct_answer: It must be in response to an advertised post
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020506 provides that transfer-on-promotion to any MDA is considered only in response to an advertised post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Under Rule 020507, an applicant may be considered for transfer if the MDA is satisfied that vacancies exist where?
option_a: In the relevant grade and in the applicant’s discipline or area of specialty
option_b: Only in the Officer’s preferred office
option_c: Only in the Staff Union office
option_d: Only in the Officer’s home town
correct_answer: In the relevant grade and in the applicant’s discipline or area of specialty
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(i)(a), the MDA must be satisfied that there are vacancies not only in the relevant grade but also in the applicant’s discipline or area of specialty.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: The contemplated transfer must not jeopardize what under Rule 020507?
option_a: The promotion prospects of serving Officers
correct_answer: The promotion prospects of serving Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(i)(b), the contemplated transfer must in no way jeopardize the promotion prospects of serving Officers.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which prior service condition must an applicant satisfy for transfer under Rule 020507?
option_a: He must have been confirmed in his previous service
option_b: He must still be on probation
option_c: He must have been dismissed previously
option_d: He must have no career progression
correct_answer: He must have been confirmed in his previous service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(i)(c), an applicant may be considered for transfer if he has been confirmed in his previous service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Under Rule 020507, the applicant’s qualifications, experience and career progression must correspond with what?
option_a: The Schemes of Service of the grade or post
correct_answer: The Schemes of Service of the grade or post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(i)(c), the applicant’s qualifications, experience and career progression must be in accordance with the Schemes of Service of the grade or post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which length-of-service condition applies before an applicant may be considered for transfer under Rule 020507?
option_a: He must have served in his current grade for the stipulated minimum number of years prescribed for promotion to an advertised post
option_b: He must have served only one week
option_c: He must have served until retirement
option_d: He must have no service record
correct_answer: He must have served in his current grade for the stipulated minimum number of years prescribed for promotion to an advertised post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(i)(d), an applicant must have served in his current grade for the stipulated minimum number of years prescribed for promotion to an advertised post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Can a Ministry transfer or second a senior Officer to a Parastatal under its supervision without approval?
option_a: No, approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board is required
option_b: Yes, it may do so without approval
option_c: Yes, if the Officer verbally agrees
option_d: Yes, if the Staff Union requests it
correct_answer: No, approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board is required
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(ii), no Ministry shall transfer or second any senior Officer to any Parastatal under its supervision without approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Can a Ministry accept staff seconded to it without endorsement of the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board?
option_a: No, it cannot accept such staff without endorsement
option_c: Yes, if the staff is on annual leave
option_d: Yes, if the staff is junior only
correct_answer: No, it cannot accept such staff without endorsement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507(iii), no Ministry shall accept any staff seconded to it without the endorsement of the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Who appraises an Officer on secondment?
option_a: The MDA to which he is seconded
correct_answer: The MDA to which he is seconded
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020507, an Officer on secondment shall be appraised by the MDA to which he is seconded.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which statement correctly summarises the conditions for transfer under Rule 020507?
option_a: There must be relevant vacancies, no harm to serving Officers’ promotion prospects, confirmation in previous service, appropriate qualifications and required years in current grade
option_b: The applicant must be unconfirmed and under discipline
option_c: The transfer must always bypass advertisement
option_d: The receiving MDA must ignore the Schemes of Service
correct_answer: There must be relevant vacancies, no harm to serving Officers’ promotion prospects, confirmation in previous service, appropriate qualifications and required years in current grade
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020507 requires relevant vacancies, protection of promotion prospects of serving Officers, confirmation in previous service, qualifications and career progression in line with the Schemes of Service, and required years in the current grade.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: How may transfer from one junior post to another within the Federal Public Service be arranged?
option_a: With the consent of the Officers and at the mutual discretion of their Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
option_b: By the Officer alone without approval
option_d: By the Staff Union without management approval
correct_answer: With the consent of the Officers and at the mutual discretion of their Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020508, transfer from one junior post to another within the Federal Public Service may be arranged with the consent of the Officers concerned and at the mutual discretion of their Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Rule 020508 applies to which category of transfer?
option_a: Transfer from one junior post to another within the Federal Public Service
option_d: Transfer-on-promotion to advertised senior posts only
correct_answer: Transfer from one junior post to another within the Federal Public Service
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020508 specifically deals with transfer from one junior post to another within the Federal Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Whose consent is required for transfer from one junior post to another?
option_a: The Officers being considered for transfer
correct_answer: The Officers being considered for transfer
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020508, the consent of the Officers being considered for transfer is required.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: What returns must MDAs make under Rule 020509?
option_a: Quarterly returns to the Federal Civil Service Commission and/or OHCSF on staff on transfer or secondment to other Services
correct_answer: Quarterly returns to the Federal Civil Service Commission and/or OHCSF on staff on transfer or secondment to other Services
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020509, MDAs shall make quarterly returns to the Federal Civil Service Commission and/or the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation on the number of staff on transfer or secondment to other Services.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: How often must MDAs make returns on staff on transfer or secondment to other Services?
option_a: Quarterly
correct_answer: Quarterly
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020509, MDAs are required to make quarterly returns on staff on transfer or secondment to other Services.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: What must the Federal Civil Service Commission furnish MDAs with on a quarterly basis?
option_a: The approved list of staff seconded or transferred to other Services
option_b: The list of Officers on annual leave only
option_c: The medical records of all Officers
option_d: The list of dismissed Officers only
correct_answer: The approved list of staff seconded or transferred to other Services
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020509, the Federal Civil Service Commission shall furnish MDAs quarterly with the approved list of staff seconded or transferred to other Services.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 5.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 5 of the PSR?
option_a: It regulates transfer and secondment, including definitions, processing authority, procedures, salary responsibility, transfer-on-promotion, conditions for transfer, junior post transfer and quarterly returns
option_b: It deals only with medical treatment abroad
option_c: It deals only with annual leave computation
option_d: It deals only with disciplinary dismissal
correct_answer: It regulates transfer and secondment, including definitions, processing authority, procedures, salary responsibility, transfer-on-promotion, conditions for transfer, junior post transfer and quarterly returns
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 5, Rules 020501 to 020509 cover transfer and secondment, including definitions, authority to process, procedure, salary responsibility, salary on transfer, transfer-on-promotion, conditions for transfer, transfer on junior posts and quarterly returns.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020601, what is posting?
option_a: A disciplinary removal from office
option_b: The initial assignment of an Officer to a position/job schedule in an MDA or reassignment within or outside his current MDA/Department
option_c: A permanent transfer from one scheduled Service to another
option_d: A temporary release to an international organization
correct_answer: The initial assignment of an Officer to a position/job schedule in an MDA or reassignment within or outside his current MDA/Department
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 6, Rule 020601, posting is the initial assignment of an Officer to a position/job schedule in an MDA or reassignment to another position/job schedule within or outside his current MDA/Department.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What is one purpose of posting under Rule 020601?
option_a: To help employees gain wide experience on the intricacies of government business
correct_answer: To help employees gain wide experience on the intricacies of government business
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020601, posting helps employees acquaint themselves with activities of various offices and gain wide experience on the intricacies of government business.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Posting may involve reassignment to another job schedule in which location?
option_a: Only within the Officer’s current Department
option_b: Only outside the Federal Public Service
option_c: Within or outside the Officer’s current MDA/Department
option_d: Only in the Officer’s home town
correct_answer: Within or outside the Officer’s current MDA/Department
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020601 provides that posting may be an initial assignment or reassignment within or outside the Officer’s current MDA/Department.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020602, senior staff may be posted or redeployed in accordance with what?
option_a: The approved Employee Mobility Policy
correct_answer: The approved Employee Mobility Policy
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020602(i), all senior staff can be posted and/or redeployed to a new post in accordance with the approved Employee Mobility Policy.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What does Rule 020602 say about posting Officers outside their Professional Cadres?
option_a: It is encouraged for all Officers
correct_answer: It is prohibited
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020602(ii), posting of Officers to posts outside their Professional Cadres is prohibited.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: How often is posting of pool Officers in the Service mandatory under Rule 020602?
option_a: Every four years
correct_answer: Every four years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020602(iii), posting of pool Officers in the Service shall be mandatory after every four years.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Failure of an Officer to proceed on posting is regarded as what under Rule 020602?
option_a: Annual leave
correct_answer: Misconduct
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020602(iv), failure of an Officer to proceed on posting shall be regarded as misconduct.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What may happen to Ministries, Extra-Ministerial Departments or Agencies that reject pool Officers deployed to them?
option_a: They may face appropriate sanctions
option_d: They are exempted from posting policy
correct_answer: They may face appropriate sanctions
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020602(iv), Ministries, Extra-Ministerial Departments or Agencies that reject pool Officers deployed to them shall face appropriate sanctions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which statement best summarises the conditions for posting under Rule 020602?
option_a: Senior staff may be posted under the Employee Mobility Policy, posting outside professional cadres is prohibited, pool Officers are posted every four years, and failure to proceed is misconduct
option_b: Only junior Officers may be posted, and posting outside professional cadres is compulsory
option_c: Posting is voluntary and cannot attract misconduct
option_d: Pool Officers may reject posting without consequence
correct_answer: Senior staff may be posted under the Employee Mobility Policy, posting outside professional cadres is prohibited, pool Officers are posted every four years, and failure to proceed is misconduct
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020602 sets the conditions for posting: senior staff may be redeployed under the Employee Mobility Policy, posting outside professional cadres is prohibited, pool Officers are posted every four years, and failure to proceed is misconduct.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What principle must guide implementation of posting decisions under Rule 020603?
option_a: Fairness to all Officers
correct_answer: Fairness to all Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020603, fairness to all Officers shall be an underlying principle in implementing posting decisions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Posting decisions must not be used as a tool for what under Rule 020603?
option_a: Coercion, punishment or cronyism
correct_answer: Coercion, punishment or cronyism
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020603, the posting system must not be used as a tool for coercion, punishment or cronyism.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020603, posting should not result in loss of what in any Department, Division or Unit?
option_a: Institutional memory
correct_answer: Institutional memory
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020603(i), posting should not result in the loss of institutional memory in any Department, Division or Unit.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Posting should not impair a Department, Division or Unit’s ability to do what?
option_a: Continue to provide quality service to internal and external stakeholders
correct_answer: Continue to provide quality service to internal and external stakeholders
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020603(i), posting should not impair the ability of any Department, Division or Unit to continue providing quality service to internal and external stakeholders.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020603, posting should not result in loss of an employee involved in what kind of project?
option_a: A service-wide project designated as high priority during the lifespan of the project
correct_answer: A service-wide project designated as high priority during the lifespan of the project
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020603(ii), posting should not result in the loss of an employee involved in any service-wide project designated as high priority during the lifespan of the project.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which statement correctly reflects the procedure for posting under Rule 020603?
option_a: Posting must be fair and must not be used for coercion, punishment or cronyism
option_b: Posting must always punish difficult Officers
option_d: Posting must remove Officers from high-priority projects at all times
correct_answer: Posting must be fair and must not be used for coercion, punishment or cronyism
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020603 requires fairness in posting decisions and prohibits using posting as a tool for coercion, punishment or cronyism.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Posting under Rule 020604 is intended to give every employee what opportunity?
option_a: Opportunity to acquire as much whole-service work experience as possible
option_c: Opportunity to remain permanently in one schedule
option_d: Opportunity to reject all pool postings
correct_answer: Opportunity to acquire as much whole-service work experience as possible
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020604, posting is to ensure every employee is given the opportunity to acquire as much of the whole-service work experience as possible.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Posting of pool staff must be done in line with what under Rule 020604?
option_a: The approved Employee Mobility Policy
correct_answer: The approved Employee Mobility Policy
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020604, posting of pool staff shall be done in line with the approved Employee Mobility Policy.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Rule 020604 mainly guides posting of which category of staff?
option_a: Pool staff
correct_answer: Pool staff
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020604, posting is to guide the posting of pool staff in line with the approved Employee Mobility Policy.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Who is expected to submit a report on compliance with posting instructions?
option_a: The Director HR
correct_answer: The Director HR
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020605, the Director HR is expected to submit a report on compliance with posting instructions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: To whom should the Director HR submit the report on compliance with posting instructions?
option_a: The relevant pool office
correct_answer: The relevant pool office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020605, the Director HR submits the report on compliance with posting instructions to the relevant pool office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Within what period must the Director HR submit the compliance report after release of posting instructions?
option_a: Within three weeks
correct_answer: Within three weeks
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020605, the Director HR shall submit the report on compliance within three weeks of the release of the posting instruction.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020606, when may an Officer seek redress over posting?
option_a: Where he believes his movement to another job or location was not done in line with extant rules
option_b: Whenever he dislikes any official instruction
option_d: Only when the posting is within the same office
correct_answer: Where he believes his movement to another job or location was not done in line with extant rules
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020606, an Officer may seek redress where he is of the opinion that his movement to another job or location was not done in line with extant rules.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Complaints or grievances on posting instructions must be submitted through what channel?
option_a: Appropriate channel
correct_answer: Appropriate channel
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020606, complaints or grievances with respect to posting instructions should be submitted through the appropriate channel.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Within what period should complaints or grievances on posting instructions be submitted after the posting is released?
option_a: Within three working days
correct_answer: Within three working days
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020606, complaints or grievances on posting instructions should be submitted through the appropriate channel within three working days of the release of the posting.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020606?
option_a: An Officer may seek redress, but must complain through appropriate channel within three working days of release of the posting
option_b: An Officer may refuse posting indefinitely without complaint
option_c: An Officer must complain only through the press
option_d: An Officer may wait six months before complaining
correct_answer: An Officer may seek redress, but must complain through appropriate channel within three working days of release of the posting
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020606, an Officer may seek redress on posting where extant rules were not followed, but complaints must be routed through appropriate channel within three working days.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Who bears the cost of entitlements due to an employee whose posting requires a change of duty station?
option_a: The posting MDA
option_b: The Officer personally in all cases
correct_answer: The posting MDA
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020607, the cost of entitlements due to the employee whose posting requires a change of duty station shall be borne by the posting MDA.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Rule 020607 applies where posting requires what?
option_a: A change of duty station
option_b: Only a change of office chair
option_c: Only a change of salary account
option_d: Only a change of leave address
correct_answer: A change of duty station
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020607, posting entitlements apply where the posting requires a change of duty station.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: An Officer who desires to live and work where his spouse lives may be allowed to do so if what condition is met?
option_a: The Branch of his MDA exists in the spouse’s location and there is a relevant established post at the Branch
option_b: The Officer simply refuses all other postings
option_c: The spouse requests it from a private employer
option_d: The Staff Union automatically approves it
correct_answer: The Branch of his MDA exists in the spouse’s location and there is a relevant established post at the Branch
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020608, an Officer may be allowed to live and work where his spouse lives if the Branch of his MDA is found in the spouse’s location and there is a relevant established post at that Branch.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What is Government’s responsibility for relocation cost when the posting is at the Officer’s request to spouse’s location?
option_a: Government is not responsible for the cost
option_c: Government pays only hotel allowance forever
correct_answer: Government is not responsible for the cost
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020608, Government shall not be responsible for the cost of relocating an Officer whose posting is at his request.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which statement correctly reflects posting to spouse’s location under Rule 020608?
option_a: It may be allowed if the Officer’s MDA has a Branch and relevant established post in the spouse’s location, but Government does not bear relocation cost if the posting is at the Officer’s request
option_b: It is automatic even where no MDA Branch exists
option_c: Government must pay all relocation costs in every case
option_d: It applies only to retired Officers
correct_answer: It may be allowed if the Officer’s MDA has a Branch and relevant established post in the spouse’s location, but Government does not bear relocation cost if the posting is at the Officer’s request
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020608 allows spouse-location posting only where the MDA has a Branch and relevant established post in the spouse’s location, and Government does not bear relocation cost where the posting is at the Officer’s request.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020609, what is the primary responsibility of Federal Government employees?
option_a: To discharge duties assigned by their employer to the Nigerian public in a timely and efficient manner
option_b: To engage only in union activities
correct_answer: To discharge duties assigned by their employer to the Nigerian public in a timely and efficient manner
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020609, the primary responsibility of all Federal Government employees is to discharge assigned duties to the Nigerian public in a timely and efficient manner.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Does involvement in staff union activities remove an Officer’s obligation to obey legitimate directives?
option_a: No, Officers must still comply with extant circulars, the PSR and legitimate directives
option_b: Yes, union activities override all official directives
option_c: Yes, union executives are exempt from the PSR
option_d: Yes, if the Officer is a union member
correct_answer: No, Officers must still comply with extant circulars, the PSR and legitimate directives
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020609, notwithstanding involvement in staff union activities, Officers remain obligated to comply with extant circulars, the PSR and legitimate directives issued by appropriate authorities.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which of the following must union executives still obey under Rule 020609?
option_a: Extant circulars, the PSR and legitimate directives issued by appropriate authorities
correct_answer: Extant circulars, the PSR and legitimate directives issued by appropriate authorities
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020609, Officers involved in staff union activities must still comply with extant circulars, the PSR and obey legitimate directives from appropriate authorities.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020610, Labour Union Executives shall not be posted out of their MDAs until when?
option_a: Until the expiration of their tenure in office
option_b: Until after one month of appointment
correct_answer: Until the expiration of their tenure in office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020610, Labour Union Executives shall not be posted out of their MDAs until the expiration of their tenure in office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which category of Officers is specifically protected from being posted out of their MDAs until tenure expiration?
option_a: Labour Union Executives
correct_answer: Labour Union Executives
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020610, Labour Union Executives shall not be posted out of their MDAs until their tenure in office expires.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: At the expiration of tenure, what must a Union Executive member not decline?
option_a: Redeployment, posting or reassignment of schedule of duties
correct_answer: Redeployment, posting or reassignment of schedule of duties
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020611, no Union Executive member at the expiration of tenure shall decline redeployment, posting or reassignment of schedule of duties.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Rule 020611 applies at what point in the Union Executive member’s service as union executive?
option_a: At the expiration of tenure in office
option_b: Before taking the oath of secrecy
correct_answer: At the expiration of tenure in office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020611, the rule applies at the expiration of the Union Executive member’s tenure in office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What tenure limit must Trade Unions and Staff Associations introduce in their Constitutions?
option_a: Two terms
correct_answer: Two terms
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020612, Trade Unions and Staff Associations are mandated to introduce a tenure limit of two terms in their Constitutions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Under Rule 020612, the duration of each union executive tenure shall not be more than what?
option_a: Two years
correct_answer: Two years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020612, the duration for each tenure shall not be more than two years.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: What is the maximum total period an Officer may serve in an executive position during his Service life?
option_a: Four years
correct_answer: Four years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020612, no Officer shall serve more than a total of four years in executive position during his Service life.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which statement correctly summarises Rule 020612?
option_a: Trade Unions and Staff Associations must limit executive tenure to two terms, each not more than two years, and no Officer may serve more than four years in executive position during Service life
option_b: Union executives may serve unlimited terms
option_c: Each union tenure must be five years
option_d: Only retired Officers may serve in union executive positions
correct_answer: Trade Unions and Staff Associations must limit executive tenure to two terms, each not more than two years, and no Officer may serve more than four years in executive position during Service life
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020612 mandates Trade Unions and Staff Associations to introduce a two-term limit, with each tenure not exceeding two years, and no Officer serving more than four years total in executive position during Service life.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 6.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 6 of the PSR?
option_a: It regulates posting of Officers, including definition, conditions, fairness, Employee Mobility Policy, compliance reports, complaints, posting entitlements, spouse-location posting and union executive posting rules
option_b: It deals only with recruitment into GL. 07–10
option_c: It deals only with confirmation examinations
option_d: It regulates only annual leave and maternity leave
correct_answer: It regulates posting of Officers, including definition, conditions, fairness, Employee Mobility Policy, compliance reports, complaints, posting entitlements, spouse-location posting and union executive posting rules
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 6, Rules 020601 to 020612 cover posting of Officers, including definition, conditions, procedure, guide to posting, Director HR reporting duty, posting complaints, entitlements, spouse-location posting, responsibilities of union executives, posting of union executives, redeployment of past union executives and tenure limits.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020701, when may an acting appointment be made?
option_a: When an Officer requests promotion
option_b: When a Staff Union recommends it
option_c: Where it is necessary for a duty post to continue to be filled and no Officer of corresponding substantive rank is available
option_d: Whenever a substantive holder takes casual leave
correct_answer: Where it is necessary for a duty post to continue to be filled and no Officer of corresponding substantive rank is available
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 7, Rule 020701, acting appointment may be made where it is necessary for a duty post to continue to be filled and no Officer of corresponding substantive rank is available for posting thereto.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What is the minimum status of the duty post contemplated under Rule 020701?
option_a: Not lower than GL. 07
correct_answer: Not lower than SGL. 14
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020701, the duty post must be of a status not lower than SGL. 14 before acting appointment may be considered.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Who must approve an acting appointment under Rule 020701?
option_a: The Officer’s colleague
option_d: The Federal Civil Service Commission or Board
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission or Board
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020701, acting appointment requires the approval of the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: How is an Officer formally appointed to act under Rule 020701?
option_a: By notice in the gazette
correct_answer: By notice in the gazette
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020701, an Officer may be formally appointed by notice in the gazette to act in the duty post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What duties may an acting Officer assume under Rule 020701?
option_a: Only ceremonial duties
option_c: Either fully or in part, the duties and responsibilities of the post
correct_answer: Either fully or in part, the duties and responsibilities of the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020701, the acting Officer may assume either fully or in part the duties and responsibilities of the duty post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020702, does short absence of a substantive holder automatically justify acting appointment?
option_a: Yes, it always justifies acting appointment
option_b: No, short absence alone does not justify acting appointment
option_c: Yes, if the Officer is on casual leave
option_d: Yes, if the Officer is on sick leave
correct_answer: No, short absence alone does not justify acting appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020702, the mere fact that the substantive holder of a duty post will be absent for a short period, such as casual leave or sick leave, does not in itself justify an acting appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which example of short absence is mentioned under Rule 020702?
option_a: Retirement after thirty-five years
correct_answer: Casual leave or sick leave
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020702, examples of short absence include casual leave or sick leave.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What circumstance may still necessitate acting appointment for a relatively brief period under Rule 020702?
option_a: Compliance with statutory provisions
option_b: Personal preference of the acting Officer
option_c: Family request of the substantive holder
correct_answer: Compliance with statutory provisions
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020702, circumstances such as compliance with statutory provisions may necessitate an acting appointment for a relatively brief period.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Who decides whether an acting appointment is necessary or desirable in a particular case?
option_a: The substantive holder alone
option_c: The Federal Civil Service Commission or Board
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission or Board
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020702, the decision whether an acting appointment is necessary or desirable rests with the Federal Civil Service Commission or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020703, acting appointment is not intended for what purpose?
option_a: To fill a temporarily vacant post
option_b: To test the suitability of Officers for promotion
option_c: To ensure continuity of official duties
option_d: To cover a vacant duty post temporarily
correct_answer: To test the suitability of Officers for promotion
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020703, acting appointment is not intended as a means of testing the suitability of Officers for promotion.
