description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Acting appointments will normally be made for what purpose under Rule 020703?
option_a: To reward staff union membership
option_d: To fill posts that are temporarily vacant
correct_answer: To fill posts that are temporarily vacant
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020703, acting appointments will normally be made only to fill posts that are temporarily vacant.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What does Rule 020703 say about the duration of acting appointments?
option_a: Their duration should be limited accordingly
correct_answer: Their duration should be limited accordingly
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020703, acting appointments are normally for temporarily vacant posts and their duration should be limited accordingly.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: On which form must recommendations for acting appointment be forwarded to the Federal Civil Service Commission?
option_a: Form L.10
correct_answer: General Form 66
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704(a), recommendations for acting appointment must be forwarded to the Federal Civil Service Commission on General Form 66.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What certificate must accompany a recommendation for acting appointment under Rule 020704?
option_a: A certificate that the acting Officer will assume the full duties and responsibilities of the post
option_b: A certificate of annual leave only
correct_answer: A certificate that the acting Officer will assume the full duties and responsibilities of the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704(a), the recommendation must include a certificate that the acting Officer will assume the full duties and responsibilities of the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Who gazettes an approved acting appointment under Rule 020704?
option_a: The Staff Union
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704(a), an approved acting appointment shall be gazetted by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: An approved acting appointment shall on no account be backdated beyond what period from the date the Commission receives the recommendation?
option_a: One year
correct_answer: Six months
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704(a), an approved acting appointment shall not be backdated to a period in excess of six months from the date the Federal Civil Service Commission receives the recommendation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What is the normal maximum period of acting appointment under Rule 020704?
option_a: Three months
correct_answer: One year
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704(b), the period of acting appointment shall not exceed one year in the normal case.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: In exceptional circumstances, an acting appointment may be extended for what additional period under Rule 020704?
option_a: Another one year
correct_answer: Another one year
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704(b), in exceptional circumstances, acting appointment may be extended for another one year.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which statement correctly summarises the procedure under Rule 020704?
option_a: Acting appointment is made by verbal instruction only
option_b: Acting appointment is unlimited once approved
option_c: Acting appointment needs no certificate or gazette
option_d: Recommendation is made on General Form 66, must include the required certificate, and approved appointment is gazetted
correct_answer: Recommendation is made on General Form 66, must include the required certificate, and approved appointment is gazetted
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020704, recommendations are forwarded on General Form 66 with the required certificate, and approved acting appointment is gazetted by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Where is the commencement date of an acting appointment indicated?
option_a: In the gazette notice authorizing the appointment
correct_answer: In the gazette notice authorizing the appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020705, the date on which an acting appointment commences is indicated in the gazette notice authorizing the appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Normally, what is the gazette date of commencement of an acting appointment?
option_a: The date the Officer applies for promotion
option_b: The date the Officer receives salary
option_c: The date the acting Officer takes over the duties and responsibilities of the post
option_d: The date the Staff Union approves it
correct_answer: The date the acting Officer takes over the duties and responsibilities of the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020705, the gazette date of commencement will normally be the date on which the acting Officer takes over the duties and responsibilities of the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Where the acting Officer takes over from the substantive holder, the gazette date of commencement will not be earlier than when?
option_a: The date the substantive holder, after handing over, leaves the station or post
option_b: The date the acting Officer first joined the Service
option_c: The date the Officer’s annual leave starts in another MDA
correct_answer: The date the substantive holder, after handing over, leaves the station or post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020705(a), where the acting Officer takes over from the substantive holder, the commencement date will not be earlier than the date the substantive holder, after handing over, leaves the station or post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which situation is listed under Rule 020705 as relevant to commencement where the substantive holder has handed over?
option_a: The substantive holder refuses to hand over
option_b: The substantive holder applies for casual leave only
option_c: The substantive holder is transferred to a private company
option_d: The substantive holder takes over substantively or acts in another post in the same station
correct_answer: The substantive holder takes over substantively or acts in another post in the same station
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020705(b), the gazette date may relate to when the substantive holder takes over substantively or acts in another post in the same station after handing over.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020705, commencement may also relate to the date the substantive holder does what in the same station?
option_a: Commences vacation leave
correct_answer: Commences vacation leave
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020705(c), the commencement date may relate to when the substantive holder commences vacation leave in the same station, where applicable.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which statement best reflects Rule 020705?
option_a: The commencement date is always the date of interview
option_b: The commencement date is fixed by the Officer alone
option_c: The commencement date is indicated in the gazette notice and normally relates to when the acting Officer takes over duties
option_d: The commencement date is never gazetted
correct_answer: The commencement date is indicated in the gazette notice and normally relates to when the acting Officer takes over duties
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020705, the commencement date is indicated in the gazette notice and normally corresponds to the date the acting Officer takes over the duties and responsibilities of the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Where is the cessation date of an acting appointment indicated under Rule 020706?
option_a: In the gazette notice reverting the Officer’s appointment
option_b: In a Staff Union register only
correct_answer: In the gazette notice reverting the Officer’s appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020706, the date on which an acting appointment ceases is indicated in the gazette notice reverting the Officer’s appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Normally, what is the gazette date of cessation of an acting appointment?
option_a: The date the Officer applied for acting appointment
option_b: The date the Officer first joined the Service
option_d: The date the acting Officer relinquishes the duties and responsibilities of the post
correct_answer: The date the acting Officer relinquishes the duties and responsibilities of the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020706, the gazette date of cessation will normally be the date on which the acting Officer relinquishes the duties and responsibilities of the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Where the acting Officer hands over to the substantive holder, the cessation date will not normally be later than when?
option_a: The date the substantive holder, before taking over, arrives at the station
option_b: The date of the next promotion exercise
option_c: The date of the acting Officer’s birthday
option_d: The date of casual leave approval
correct_answer: The date the substantive holder, before taking over, arrives at the station
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020706(a), where the acting Officer hands over to the substantive holder, the cessation date will not normally be later than the date the substantive holder, before taking over, arrives at the station.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which event is listed under Rule 020706 as relevant before the substantive holder takes over?
option_a: The substantive holder receives annual allowance only
option_b: The substantive holder joins the Staff Union
option_c: The substantive holder ceases to hold substantively or acts in another post in the same station
option_d: The substantive holder starts a private business
correct_answer: The substantive holder ceases to hold substantively or acts in another post in the same station
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020706(b), the cessation date may relate to when the substantive holder ceases to hold substantively or acts in another post in the same station before taking over.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020706, cessation may also relate to when the substantive holder does what in the same station?
option_a: Ceases vacation leave
correct_answer: Ceases vacation leave
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020706(c), the cessation date may relate to when the substantive holder ceases vacation leave in the same station, where applicable.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which statement best summarises Rule 020706?
option_a: Acting appointment ceases only when the Staff Union decides
option_b: Acting appointment ceases without gazette notice
option_c: Acting appointment ceases only at retirement
option_d: Cessation is indicated in the gazette notice reverting the Officer and normally relates to relinquishing the duties of the post
correct_answer: Cessation is indicated in the gazette notice reverting the Officer and normally relates to relinquishing the duties of the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020706, the cessation date is indicated in the gazette notice reverting the Officer and normally corresponds to the date the acting Officer relinquishes the duties and responsibilities of the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020707, Ministries must notify whom when Officers revert from acting appointment?
option_a: The Officer’s family
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020707, Ministries are required to notify the Federal Civil Service Commission when Officers revert from acting appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which form is used to notify the Federal Civil Service Commission when Officers revert from acting appointment?
option_a: Form Gen. 15A
correct_answer: Form Gen. 15A
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020707, notification of reversion from acting appointment is done by completing Form No. Gen. 15A.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: When must Form Gen. 15A be forwarded before cessation of acting appointment?
option_a: Not less than two weeks before cessation
correct_answer: Not less than two weeks before cessation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020707, Form No. Gen. 15A must be forwarded not less than two weeks before cessation of the acting appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020707?
option_a: Ministries notify the Staff Union by casual leave form
option_b: Ministries need not notify anyone when acting appointment ends
option_c: Ministries notify the FCSC after five years only
option_d: Ministries notify the FCSC by Form Gen. 15A not less than two weeks before cessation
correct_answer: Ministries notify the FCSC by Form Gen. 15A not less than two weeks before cessation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020707, Ministries must notify the Federal Civil Service Commission by completing Form Gen. 15A and forwarding it not less than two weeks before cessation of the acting appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Under Rule 020708, does an acting Officer relinquish acting duties merely by proceeding on casual or special leave within Nigeria?
option_a: Yes, always
option_b: Only if the leave is one day
option_c: No, provided the stated conditions are satisfied
option_d: Only if the Officer is a union executive
correct_answer: No, provided the stated conditions are satisfied
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020708(a), an acting Officer is not regarded as relinquishing acting duties by proceeding on casual or special leave within the country, provided the stated conditions are met.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: For casual or special leave not to amount to relinquishment under Rule 020708, where must the acting Officer spend the leave?
option_a: In Nigeria or on a sea voyage between Nigerian ports
option_b: In any foreign country without approval
option_c: Only in the substantive holder’s house
correct_answer: In Nigeria or on a sea voyage between Nigerian ports
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020708(a), the acting Officer must spend such leave in Nigeria or on a sea voyage between Nigerian ports.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which additional condition applies under Rule 020708(a) for casual or special leave not to amount to relinquishment?
option_a: It must be necessary to appoint another Officer to act
option_b: The acting Officer must refuse to resume duty
option_c: The acting Officer must apply for promotion
option_d: It must not be necessary during such leave to appoint another Officer to act in the duty post
correct_answer: It must not be necessary during such leave to appoint another Officer to act in the duty post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020708(a), casual or special leave will not amount to relinquishment provided it is not necessary during such leave to appoint another Officer to act in the duty post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Where the Head of a Department, Division, Unit or Branch is unavailable for a period spanning one month, who oversees the office?
option_a: The most junior Officer
option_c: The most senior Officer in the Department or Organization
correct_answer: The most senior Officer in the Department or Organization
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020708(b), where the Head of a Department, Division, Unit or Branch is unavailable for a period spanning one month, the most senior Officer in the Department or Organization shall oversee the office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Rule 020708(b) applies where the Head of Department, Division, Unit or Branch is unavailable due to what?
option_a: Annual leave or any other approved assignment
correct_answer: Annual leave or any other approved assignment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020708(b), the provision applies where the Head is unavailable for a period spanning one month as a result of annual leave or any other approved assignment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: What period of unavailability triggers the arrangement under Rule 020708(b)?
option_a: A period spanning one month
correct_answer: A period spanning one month
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020708(b), where the Head of Department, Division, Unit or Branch is unavailable for a period spanning one month, the most senior Officer shall oversee the office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 7.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 7 of the PSR?
option_a: It deals only with annual leave
option_b: It deals only with transfer and secondment
option_c: It deals only with recruitment of junior staff
option_d: It regulates acting appointment, including when it is made, approval, gazetting, procedure, commencement, cessation, FCSC notification and the effect of casual or special leave
correct_answer: It regulates acting appointment, including when it is made, approval, gazetting, procedure, commencement, cessation, FCSC notification and the effect of casual or special leave
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 7, Rules 020701 to 020708 regulate acting appointment, including when it may be made, when it is not justified, procedure, commencement, cessation, notification to the Federal Civil Service Commission and the effect of casual or special leave.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020801, promotion to all posts in the Federal Civil Service, except Permanent Secretaries, is vested in which authority?
option_a: The Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 8, Rule 020801, promotion to all posts in the Federal Civil Service, other than those of Permanent Secretaries, is vested in the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which post is expressly excluded from the general promotion authority stated in Rule 020801(a)?
option_a: Permanent Secretaries
correct_answer: Permanent Secretaries
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020801(a) states that promotion to all posts other than those of Permanent Secretaries is vested in the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020801(b), Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices may promote eligible candidates to which delegated posts?
option_a: All posts up to GL. 17
option_c: Posts on SGL 06 or its equivalent and below
correct_answer: Posts on SGL 06 or its equivalent and below
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020801(b), Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices may promote eligible candidates to delegated posts on SGL 06 or its equivalent and below.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Promotion by Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices under Rule 020801(b) must be based on what?
option_a: Private recommendation of the Officer
correct_answer: Recommendation of the appropriate committee
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020801(b), promotion to delegated posts on SGL 06 or equivalent and below is based on the recommendation of the appropriate committee.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Except where powers have been delegated, when does a promotion become effective under Rule 020802(a)?
option_a: When the Officer applies for it
option_b: When the Staff Union supports it
option_d: When approved by the Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: When approved by the Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(a), except where powers of appointment or promotion have been delegated, no promotion becomes effective until approved by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020802(b), which Officers within the field of selection shall not be considered for promotion?
option_a: Officers under disciplinary action
option_d: Officers who are due for promotion
correct_answer: Officers under disciplinary action
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(b), all Officers within the field of selection shall be considered except those who are under disciplinary action.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the minimum number of years in post for Officers on GL. 06 and below before promotion consideration under Rule 020802(c)?
option_a: Minimum of 4 years
correct_answer: Minimum of 2 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(c), Officers on GL. 06 and below must spend a minimum of 2 years in post before being considered eligible for promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the minimum number of years in post for Officers on GL. 07–14 before promotion consideration under Rule 020802(c)?
option_a: Minimum of 2 years
correct_answer: Minimum of 3 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(c), Officers on GL. 07–14 must spend a minimum of 3 years in post before being considered eligible for promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: What is the minimum number of years in post for Officers on GL. 15–17 before promotion consideration under Rule 020802(c)?
option_a: Minimum of 2 years
correct_answer: Minimum of 4 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(c), Officers on GL. 15–17 must spend a minimum of 4 years in post before being considered eligible for promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Promotion under Rule 020802(d) must be made strictly on what basis?
option_a: Competitive merit
correct_answer: Competitive merit
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(d), promotion shall be made strictly on the basis of competitive merit from among all eligible candidates.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: In assessing merit under Rule 020802(d), what distinction must be made?
option_a: Between salary and pension only
option_b: Between lower-grade performance or efficiency and potential for the higher post
option_d: Between Officers who live near and far from office
correct_answer: Between lower-grade performance or efficiency and potential for the higher post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(d)(i), a clear distinction must be made between records of performance or efficiency in lower grades and potential to perform higher duties efficiently.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020802(d), seniority and previous performance records are used especially when candidates have what?
option_a: No qualification at all
correct_answer: Equal potential for promotion
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(d)(ii), seniority and previous records of performance are taken into account in choosing between candidates with equal potential for promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which conduct requirement is considered in all promotion cases under Rule 020802(d)?
option_a: Ability to travel abroad
option_d: A generally satisfactory record of conduct
correct_answer: A generally satisfactory record of conduct
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(d)(iii), a generally satisfactory record of conduct shall be considered in all promotion cases.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who is responsible for promotion of Officers into GL. 06 or its equivalent and below under Rule 020802(e)?
option_a: The National Assembly
correct_answer: The Ministry, Department and Agency
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(e)(i), promotion into GL. 06 or its equivalent and below is by the Ministry, Department and Agency.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Promotion into GL. 07 to SGL 14 is handled by the Ministry or relevant staff pool with whose approval, subject to confirmation by the FCSC or Board?
option_a: The Staff Union Chairman
option_c: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(e)(ii), promotion into GL. 07 to SGL 14 is by the Ministry or relevant staff pool with approval of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, subject to confirmation by the FCSC or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Promotion into GL. 15–17 is by the Federal Civil Service Commission on recommendation routed through which office or authority?
option_a: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation or Board
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation or Board
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(e)(iii), promotion into GL. 15–17 is by the Federal Civil Service Commission on recommendation routed through the OHCSF or Board.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020802(f), all promotion is subject to minimum requirements and what else?
option_a: The Officer’s private request
correct_answer: Availability of vacancies
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(f), all promotion is subject to satisfying minimum requirements declared by the FCSC or Board and to availability of vacancies.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Before enlisting Officers for promotion examination, Heads of MDAs must submit their approved establishment for the year to whom?
option_a: The Officer’s union branch
option_b: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(g), Heads of MDAs must submit their approved establishment for the year to the OHCSF before enlisting Officers for promotion examination.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Why must Heads of MDAs submit their approved establishment before promotion examination under Rule 020802(g)?
option_a: To determine annual leave balances
option_c: To ensure promotion falls in line with existing vacancies
option_d: To avoid using the Schemes of Service
correct_answer: To ensure promotion falls in line with existing vacancies
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020802(g), approved establishment is submitted before promotion examination to ensure that promotion falls in line with existing vacancies.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects eligibility under Rule 020802(b)?
option_a: All Officers in the field of selection are considered except those under disciplinary action
option_b: Only Officers under disciplinary action are considered
option_c: Only Officers on leave are considered
correct_answer: All Officers in the field of selection are considered except those under disciplinary action
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020802(b) provides that all Officers in the field of selection shall be considered except those under disciplinary action.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Before each promotion exercise, what must the appropriate Office compile under Rule 020803?
option_a: A list of all eligible candidates to be considered
option_b: A list of all retired Officers only
option_c: A list of disciplinary cases only
correct_answer: A list of all eligible candidates to be considered
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803, before each promotion exercise, the appropriate Office shall compile a list of all eligible candidates to be considered.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: The list of eligible candidates under Rule 020803 is prepared on what basis?
option_a: The Officer’s family background
option_c: Job requirements or criteria established for the post
correct_answer: Job requirements or criteria established for the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803, the list is prepared on the basis of job requirements or set criteria established for the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who establishes the job requirements or criteria for the post under Rule 020803?
option_a: The Officer’s colleague
option_d: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
correct_answer: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803, the job requirements or criteria for the post are established by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which of the following is listed as an example of criteria under Rule 020803?
option_a: Qualification, experience, age, training and performance
correct_answer: Qualification, experience, age, training and performance
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803, examples of criteria include qualification, experience, age, training and performance as contained in the Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: The promotion criteria under Rule 020803 must be as contained in what document?
option_a: The Officer’s private diary
correct_answer: The Schemes of Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803, the criteria for promotion are those contained in the Schemes of Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: What type of training is required for career progression under Rule 020803(a)?
option_a: Unstructured private coaching only
correct_answer: Structured and sustained training
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803(a), there shall be structured and sustained training for career progression in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Structured and sustained training under Rule 020803 includes what?
option_a: Compulsory annual leave only
correct_answer: Continuous professional training and development
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803(a), structured and sustained training includes continuous professional training and development.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Officers qualify for promotion to a higher grade after acquiring what under Rule 020803(b)?
option_a: Political endorsement only
option_b: Skill and competence provided in the Schemes of Service for the cadre
correct_answer: Skill and competence provided in the Schemes of Service for the cadre
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803(b), Officers qualify for promotion after acquiring the skill and competence provided in the Schemes of Service for the particular cadre.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020803, who compiles the list of eligible candidates before promotion exercise?
option_a: The appropriate Office
correct_answer: The appropriate Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020803, the appropriate Office compiles the list of all eligible candidates before each promotion exercise.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020804, who interviews and considers Officers holding junior appointments for promotion from junior to senior post?
option_a: The Officer’s family
correct_answer: The appropriate committee
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020804, the appropriate committee meets to interview and consider Officers holding junior appointments who may be recommended for promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Officers holding junior appointments may be recommended to which body under Rule 020804?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020804, Officers holding junior appointments may be recommended to the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: What does the Federal Civil Service Commission do after receiving recommendations under Rule 020804?
option_a: It automatically rejects all junior Officers
option_b: It sends them for annual leave only
option_c: It examines suitability and offers promotion to existing vacancies
option_d: It refers them to private employers
correct_answer: It examines suitability and offers promotion to existing vacancies
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020804, the Federal Civil Service Commission examines the suitability of recommended Officers and offers them promotion to existing vacancies.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020805, vacancies on GL. 06 and below are filled by Permanent Secretaries or Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices on whose recommendation?
option_a: The Minister’s driver
correct_answer: The Junior Staff Committee
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020805, Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices fill vacancies on GL. 06 and below on the recommendation of the Junior Staff Committee.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 020805 applies to vacancies on which grade level range?
option_a: GL. 15–17 only
correct_answer: GL. 06 and below
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020805, vacancies on posts on GL. 06 and below are filled on the recommendation of the Junior Staff Committee.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which committee recommends the filling of vacancies from one junior post to another under Rule 020805?
option_a: Junior Staff Committee
correct_answer: Junior Staff Committee
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020805, vacancies on GL. 06 and below are filled on the recommendation of the Junior Staff Committee.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020806, what is the effective date of all promotions?
option_a: The date the Officer submits an application
option_b: The date of the interview only
option_c: 1st January of the year for which the promotion exercise was conducted or as determined by the FCSC
correct_answer: 1st January of the year for which the promotion exercise was conducted or as determined by the FCSC
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020806, the effective date of all promotions is 1st January of the year for which the promotion exercise was conducted or as may be determined by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who may determine an effective date different from 1st January under Rule 020806?
option_a: The Federal Civil Service Commission
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020806, the effective date is 1st January of the promotion exercise year or as may be determined by the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020806?
option_a: Promotion takes effect only on the Officer’s birthday
option_b: Promotion takes effect on 1st January of the relevant promotion exercise year or as determined by the FCSC
option_c: Promotion takes effect only after retirement
option_d: Promotion takes effect whenever the Officer chooses
correct_answer: Promotion takes effect on 1st January of the relevant promotion exercise year or as determined by the FCSC
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020806 provides that the effective date of all promotions shall be 1st January of the year for which the promotion exercise was conducted or as determined by the FCSC.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020807, Officers on approved leave of absence, secondment, approved study leave or special assignment shall sit for promotion interviews or examinations where?
option_a: Only at their original headquarters
option_c: Only after returning from the assignment
option_d: At designated centres nearest to them
correct_answer: At designated centres nearest to them
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020807, such Officers shall sit for promotion interviews or examinations at designated centres nearest to them.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which category of Officers is covered by Rule 020807?
option_a: Officers on approved leave of absence, secondment, approved study leave or special assignment
correct_answer: Officers on approved leave of absence, secondment, approved study leave or special assignment
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020807 covers Officers on approved leave of absence, secondment, approved study leave or special assignment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: What does Rule 020807 require of eligible Officers on approved absence or assignment?
option_a: They are automatically exempted from promotion examination
option_c: They shall sit for promotion interviews or examinations at designated centres nearest to them
option_d: They may be promoted without any process
correct_answer: They shall sit for promotion interviews or examinations at designated centres nearest to them
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020807, Officers on approved leave of absence, secondment, approved study leave or special assignment shall sit for promotion interviews or examinations at designated centres nearest to them.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020808, a newly recruited Officer who has spent how long may sit for compulsory confirmation examination?
option_a: Six months and above
correct_answer: Six months and above
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020808, a newly recruited Officer who has spent six months and above shall be allowed to sit for compulsory examination for confirmation in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: The compulsory confirmation examination under Rule 020808 is allowed pending completion of what period?
option_a: Three months of casual leave
correct_answer: Probationary period of two years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020808, the Officer may sit for the examination pending completion of the probationary period of two years in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: What examination may a newly recruited Officer sit for after six months and above under Rule 020808?
option_a: Promotion interview only
correct_answer: Compulsory examination for confirmation
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020808, a newly recruited Officer who has spent six months and above may sit for compulsory examination for confirmation in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020809, may a contract Officer be considered for promotion?
option_a: Yes, automatically every year
option_c: No, a contract Officer shall not be considered for promotion
option_d: Yes, if the Staff Union recommends him
correct_answer: No, a contract Officer shall not be considered for promotion
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020809, no contract Officer shall be considered for promotion.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Although a contract Officer is not considered for promotion, what may he be considered for under Rule 020809?
option_a: Automatic pensionable appointment
option_d: Enhanced appointment during re-negotiation of his contract
correct_answer: Enhanced appointment during re-negotiation of his contract
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020809, a contract Officer may be considered for enhanced appointment during the re-negotiation of his contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020809?
option_a: A contract Officer may be considered for enhanced appointment during contract re-negotiation, but not promotion
option_b: A contract Officer must be promoted annually
option_c: A contract Officer is automatically converted to Permanent Secretary
option_d: A contract Officer cannot have contract terms reviewed
correct_answer: A contract Officer may be considered for enhanced appointment during contract re-negotiation, but not promotion
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020809 provides that no contract Officer shall be considered for promotion, but he may be considered for enhanced appointment during re-negotiation of his contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020810, promotion of junior and senior Officers in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies is invalid without whose representatives?
option_a: The Staff Union and Pension Fund Administrator
option_b: Human Resource Management of the supervising Ministry and OHCSF
option_c: The Officer’s family and private employer
correct_answer: Human Resource Management of the supervising Ministry and OHCSF
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020810, promotion of junior and senior Officers in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies is invalid without representatives of the Human Resource Management of the supervising Ministry and OHCSF.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 020810 applies to promotion of which Officers in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies?
option_a: Only retired Officers
correct_answer: Junior and senior Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020810, the rule applies to promotion of both junior and senior Officers in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Promotion under Rule 020810 concerns which type of organization?
option_a: Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies
correct_answer: Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020810, the validity requirement applies to promotion in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020810?
option_a: Promotion in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies is deemed invalid without HRM representatives of the supervising Ministry and OHCSF
option_b: Promotion in Parastatals is valid without any representative
option_c: Only the Officer’s family validates promotion
option_d: Promotion in Parastatals is not covered by the PSR
correct_answer: Promotion in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies is deemed invalid without HRM representatives of the supervising Ministry and OHCSF
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020810 states that promotion of junior and senior Officers in Federal Government Parastatals or Agencies is invalid without representatives of the HRM of the supervising Ministry and OHCSF.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: To be eligible for the Permanent Secretary appointment process, a candidate must be what grade and stream under Rule 020811(a)?
option_a: GL. 06 Officer in a junior cadre
option_c: Director on GL. 17 in the mainstream of the Federal Civil Service
correct_answer: Director on GL. 17 in the mainstream of the Federal Civil Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(a), the candidate must be a Director on GL. 17 and in the mainstream of the Federal Civil Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020811(b), the candidate must be verified on IPPIS as having what status?
option_a: Unconfirmed trainee status
option_b: Confirmed staff of the Federal Government of Nigeria
correct_answer: Confirmed staff of the Federal Government of Nigeria
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(b), the candidate must have been verified on the IPPIS portal or platform as confirmed staff of the Federal Government of Nigeria.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: How long must a candidate have been on the post of Director to qualify under Rule 020811(c)?
option_a: At least two years
correct_answer: At least two years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(c), a candidate must be at least two years on the post of Director.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020811(d), which retirement condition affects eligibility for the Permanent Secretary appointment process?
option_a: The candidate must be retiring immediately
option_b: The candidate must have already retired
option_c: The candidate must be on terminal leave
option_d: The candidate must not be retiring on or before 31st December of the following year
correct_answer: The candidate must not be retiring on or before 31st December of the following year
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(d), the candidate must not be retiring on or before 31st December of the following year.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: What proof must a candidate provide under Rule 020811(e)?
option_a: Proof of annual leave
option_b: Proof of indigeneship of the State where vacancy exists
option_d: Proof of membership of a Staff Union
correct_answer: Proof of indigeneship of the State where vacancy exists
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(e), the candidate must provide proof of indigeneship of the State where the vacancy exists.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: For a female Civil Servant, indigeneship of a State under Rule 020811(f) must not be by what?
option_a: Birth
correct_answer: Marriage
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(f), indigeneship of a State must not be by marriage in the case of a female Civil Servant.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which disciplinary condition applies under Rule 020811(g)?
option_a: The candidate must not have a pending disciplinary action
option_b: The candidate must be under disciplinary action
option_c: The candidate must have been dismissed before
option_d: The candidate must have refused promotion examination
correct_answer: The candidate must not have a pending disciplinary action
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(g), the candidate must not have a pending disciplinary action against him.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which option best lists key eligibility criteria for Permanent Secretary appointment under Rule 020811?
option_a: Contract status, private employment and annual leave
option_b: Union office, overseas posting and medical leave
option_c: Junior post, unpaid appointment and acting allowance
option_d: GL. 17 Director in mainstream Federal Civil Service, confirmed on IPPIS, two years as Director, required indigeneship, and no pending disciplinary action
correct_answer: GL. 17 Director in mainstream Federal Civil Service, confirmed on IPPIS, two years as Director, required indigeneship, and no pending disciplinary action
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811, eligibility includes being a GL. 17 Director in the mainstream Federal Civil Service, IPPIS-confirmed, at least two years as Director, proof of indigeneship where vacancy exists, and no pending disciplinary action.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 020811 sets eligibility criteria for participation in what process?
option_a: Appointment process of Permanent Secretaries
correct_answer: Appointment process of Permanent Secretaries
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020811 sets the eligibility criteria for participating in the appointment process of Permanent Secretaries in the Federal Civil Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020811, the candidate for Permanent Secretary must be a Director in which Service?
option_a: The mainstream of the Federal Civil Service
correct_answer: The mainstream of the Federal Civil Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020811(a), the candidate must be a Director on GL. 17 in the mainstream of the Federal Civil Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020812, selection for Permanent Secretary shall be through what type of process?
option_a: Private nomination only
correct_answer: Competitive examination process
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020812, selection shall be through a competitive examination process.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which assessment is specifically included in the selection process under Rule 020812?
option_a: Written examination
correct_answer: Written examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020812, the competitive examination process includes written examination.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 020812 includes a test of what proficiency?
option_a: Driving proficiency
correct_answer: ICT proficiency
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020812, the competitive examination process includes a test of ICT proficiency.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which of the following is included in the selection process under Rule 020812?
option_a: Private family interview only
correct_answer: Oral interview
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020812, the competitive examination process includes oral interview.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best reflects the phrase “including but not limited to” in Rule 020812?
option_a: The process may include written examination, ICT proficiency test, oral interview and other relevant assessments
option_b: The process is limited to Staff Union approval
option_d: The process is only a medical check
correct_answer: The process may include written examination, ICT proficiency test, oral interview and other relevant assessments
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020812, selection is through a competitive examination process including but not limited to written examination, test of ICT proficiency and oral interview.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020813, resource persons may come from which sources?
option_a: Only the Officer’s family
option_c: Civil or Public Service and private institutions
correct_answer: Civil or Public Service and private institutions
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020813, resource persons from the Civil or Public Service and private institutions may be involved in the selection process.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Resource persons under Rule 020813 may be involved in what?
option_a: The selection process
correct_answer: The selection process
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020813, resource persons from the Civil or Public Service and private institutions may be involved in the selection process.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 8, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 8 of the PSR?
option_a: It deals only with annual leave and maternity leave
option_b: It regulates medical treatment and burial expenses only
option_c: It applies only to disciplinary dismissal
option_d: It regulates promotion authority, eligibility, merit criteria, promotion procedures, effective date, approved-absence examination arrangements, contract Officers, parastatal promotion validity and Permanent Secretary selection criteria
correct_answer: It regulates promotion authority, eligibility, merit criteria, promotion procedures, effective date, approved-absence examination arrangements, contract Officers, parastatal promotion validity and Permanent Secretary selection criteria
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 8, Rules 020801 to 020813 cover promotion authority, eligibility, merit criteria, procedure, promotion from junior to senior posts, effective date, Officers on approved absence, contract Officers, parastatal promotion validity and Permanent Secretary selection criteria.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020901, when may the appointment of an Officer on probation be terminated?
option_a: Only after thirty-five years of service
option_b: When the appointing authority is satisfied that the Officer is not qualified for efficient service
option_c: Only when the Officer applies for annual leave
correct_answer: When the appointing authority is satisfied that the Officer is not qualified for efficient service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, if within the probationary period the appointing authority is satisfied that an Officer is not qualified for efficient service, the appointment may be terminated.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who may terminate the appointment of an Officer on probation under Rule 020901?
option_a: The Officer’s colleague
option_c: The authority empowered to appoint the Officer
correct_answer: The authority empowered to appoint the Officer
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, the authority empowered to appoint the Officer may terminate the appointment during probation where the stated condition is met.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: What compensation is generally available to a probationary Officer whose appointment is terminated under Rule 020901?
option_a: Free transport to the place from which he was engaged, subject to good conduct
correct_answer: Free transport to the place from which he was engaged, subject to good conduct
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, the Officer receives no further compensation than free transport to the place from which he was engaged, and this is granted only if his conduct has been good.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Free transport under Rule 020901 is granted only if what condition is satisfied?
option_a: The Officer has served for 35 years
option_c: The Officer’s conduct has been good
correct_answer: The Officer’s conduct has been good
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, free transport is granted only where the Officer’s conduct has been good.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: If termination of a probationary appointment is not due to misconduct, how is it effected under Rule 020901?
option_a: By immediate dismissal without notice
correct_answer: By one month’s notice
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, where termination is not due to misconduct, it is effected by one month’s notice.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020901, what may be granted to an eligible probationary Officer in respect of service to date?
option_a: Vacation leave
correct_answer: Vacation leave
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, if the Officer is eligible for vacation leave in respect of service to date, such leave may be granted.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: How should leave granted under Rule 020901 be arranged where possible?
option_a: To begin after retirement only
option_c: To take place within the period of notice and, if possible, expire on the same day as the notice
option_d: To be accumulated for the next year
correct_answer: To take place within the period of notice and, if possible, expire on the same day as the notice
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020901, leave granted in this situation should be arranged within the notice period and, if possible, expire on the same day as the notice.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020901, what governs the refund of the cost of training given to the Officer?
option_a: The bond relating to the training
correct_answer: The bond relating to the training
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020901 states that refund of the cost of any training given to the Officer is governed by the bond relating to such training.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which statement best reflects termination during probation under Rule 020901?
option_a: It is always treated as promotion
option_b: It may occur where the appointing authority is satisfied that the Officer is not qualified for efficient service
option_c: It can only be approved by the Officer himself
correct_answer: It may occur where the appointing authority is satisfied that the Officer is not qualified for efficient service
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020901 allows termination during probation where the appointing authority is satisfied that the Officer is not qualified for efficient service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020902, what may an Officer who relinquishes appointment during probation be required to refund?
option_a: Annual leave allowance only
option_b: Government expenditure on transporting his family, servant and baggage to and from the place of employment
correct_answer: Government expenditure on transporting his family, servant and baggage to and from the place of employment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020902, an Officer who relinquishes appointment during probation may be required to refund Government expenditure on transporting his family, servant and baggage to and from the place where he was employed.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: An Officer who relinquishes appointment during probation is not eligible for what under Rule 020902?
option_a: Government transport facilities from the station where he was serving
option_c: Staff identity card before assumption of duty
correct_answer: Government transport facilities from the station where he was serving
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020902, the Officer will not be eligible for any facilities from Government towards transport from the station where he was serving.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 020902 applies to relinquishment of appointment during which period?
option_a: After compulsory retirement
option_c: After serving as Director for eight years
correct_answer: During probationary service
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020902 applies where an Officer relinquishes his appointment within the period of probationary service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020902, refund of training cost is governed by what?
option_a: The bond relating to such training
correct_answer: The bond relating to such training
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020902, refund of the cost of any training given to the Officer is governed by the bond relating to such training.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly describes the transport consequence under Rule 020902?
option_a: The Officer is automatically entitled to free transport after relinquishment
option_b: The Officer may be required to refund Government transport expenditure and is not eligible for further Government transport facilities from the station
option_c: The Officer receives international passage for his family
option_d: The Officer receives transport grant for four years
correct_answer: The Officer may be required to refund Government transport expenditure and is not eligible for further Government transport facilities from the station
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020902 provides that an Officer who relinquishes appointment during probation may refund Government transport expenditure and is not eligible for Government transport facilities from the station of service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020903, what may happen to a probationary Officer who fails to secure confirmation in the pensionable establishment?
option_a: His appointment may be terminated
option_d: He is placed on sabbatical leave
correct_answer: His appointment may be terminated
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020903, the appointment of an Officer on probation who fails to secure confirmation in the pensionable establishment may be terminated.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Failure to secure confirmation under Rule 020903 is assessed at what point?
option_a: At the expiration of the probationary period, including any prescribed extension
correct_answer: At the expiration of the probationary period, including any prescribed extension
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020903, termination may occur where confirmation is not secured at the expiration of the probationary period, including such extension as prescribed under Rule 020301.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 020903 refers to extension of probation as prescribed under which rule?
option_a: Rule 020301
correct_answer: Rule 020301
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020903, the probationary period includes any extension prescribed under Rule 020301.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: The termination of an Officer under Rule 020903 is to be done in the manner specified in which rule?
option_a: Rule 020801
correct_answer: Rule 020901
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020903 states that termination for failure to secure confirmation is done in the manner specified in Rule 020901.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020904, what happens to an Officer who resigns in relation to vacation leave claims?
option_a: He forfeits all claims to vacation leave
correct_answer: He forfeits all claims to vacation leave
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020904, an Officer who resigns is liable to forfeit all claims to vacation leave.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Where vacation leave or passage privileges are granted to an Officer who resigns, how are they treated under Rule 020904?
option_a: As statutory entitlement in all cases
correct_answer: As ex-gratia
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020904, any vacation leave or passage privileges granted to an Officer who resigns are ex-gratia.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020904, what must a resigning Officer refund to Government?
option_a: Any sum owed to Government or refundable under rules or agreements
option_b: Only the cost of staff identity card
correct_answer: Any sum owed to Government or refundable under rules or agreements
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020904, a resigning Officer must refund in full any sum owed to Government or refundable under rules or agreements entered into with Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Why may a resigning Officer be required to refund money under Rule 020904?
option_a: For not discharging obligations set out in an agreement with Government
option_b: For taking annual leave in December
correct_answer: For not discharging obligations set out in an agreement with Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020904, refund may be required where money is refundable for not discharging obligations set out in an agreement with Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who may waive any or all refunds due from a resigning Officer under Rule 020904?
option_a: Government
correct_answer: Government
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020904 provides that any or all such refunds may be waived at the discretion of the Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly summarises resignation under Rule 020904?
option_a: Resignation always gives automatic pension and leave accumulation
option_b: Resignation makes the Officer liable to forfeit vacation leave claims and refund sums owed or refundable to Government
option_d: Resignation automatically converts the Officer to contract staff
correct_answer: Resignation makes the Officer liable to forfeit vacation leave claims and refund sums owed or refundable to Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020904, a resigning Officer forfeits vacation leave claims and must refund sums owed or refundable to Government, subject to possible waiver by Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020905, an Officer who leaves the Service other than by resignation or dismissal is eligible for what?
option_a: Proportionate leave in accordance with Rule 120212
correct_answer: Proportionate leave in accordance with Rule 120212
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020905, an Officer who leaves the Service other than by resignation or dismissal is eligible for proportionate leave in accordance with Rule 120212.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 020905 excludes which two modes of leaving Service from its proportionate leave provision?
option_a: Transfer and secondment
correct_answer: Resignation and dismissal
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020905 applies to an Officer who leaves the Service other than by resignation or dismissal.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: If an Officer has enjoyed more leave during the leave year than he is eligible to receive, what is required under Rule 020905?
option_a: He must refund salary for the excess working days’ leave enjoyed
option_b: He must receive additional leave allowance
option_d: He must repeat the leave year
correct_answer: He must refund salary for the excess working days’ leave enjoyed
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020905, an Officer who has enjoyed excess leave must refund salary for the number of working days’ leave enjoyed in excess of eligibility.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 1 of 2.
question: For pension purposes, days for which salary is refunded under Rule 020905 are treated as what?
option_a: Sick leave with pay
correct_answer: Leave without pay
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020905, days for which salary is refunded are treated as leave without pay for pension purposes.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: In which case is the refund provision under Rule 020905 waived?
option_a: Where the Officer dies in the Service
correct_answer: Where the Officer dies in the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020905, the refund provision is waived in the case of an Officer who dies in the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which rule is specifically referenced for proportionate leave under Rule 020905?
option_a: Rule 120212
correct_answer: Rule 120212
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020905 provides that proportionate leave is determined in accordance with Rule 120212.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020906, an Officer who fails promotion examinations after how many consecutive attempts is deemed to have exited the Service?
option_a: One consecutive attempt
correct_answer: Three consecutive attempts
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, Officers who fail promotion examinations after three consecutive attempts are deemed to have exited the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020906, an Officer who refuses or fails to write promotion examination for the third time on unacceptable grounds is deemed to have done what?
option_a: Exited from the Service
correct_answer: Exited from the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, an Officer who absents himself from an examination on unacceptable grounds is deemed to have exited the Service when he refuses to write the examination the third time.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: For absence from promotion examination on grounds of ill-health to be acceptable under Rule 020906, what is required?
option_a: A medical report from a recognized Healthcare Provider
option_b: A verbal message from a colleague
correct_answer: A medical report from a recognized Healthcare Provider
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, absence on grounds of ill-health must be supported by a medical report from a recognized Healthcare Provider.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020906, reasons for absence other than ill-health are evaluated by whom?
option_a: The Officer’s family
correct_answer: The Federal Civil Service Commission
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, other reasons for absence from the examination are based on the evaluation of the Federal Civil Service Commission.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: How should Officers who score below the pass mark in a promotion examination be notified under Rule 020906?
option_a: Either in writing or by messages sent to their given e-mail address
option_b: Only by public announcement in a market
correct_answer: Either in writing or by messages sent to their given e-mail address
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, Officers who score below the pass mark are notified either in writing or by messages sent to their given e-mail address.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who gives the notification to Officers that scored below the pass mark under Rule 020906?
option_a: The authority that conducted the examination
correct_answer: The authority that conducted the examination
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, notification to Officers who scored below the pass mark is given by the authority that conducted the examination.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: At what point is an Officer deemed to have exited after failing promotion examinations under Rule 020906?
option_a: After the failed third consecutive attempt
correct_answer: After the failed third consecutive attempt
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020906, the Officer is deemed to have exited the Service after the failed third consecutive attempt.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 020906?
option_a: Failure of promotion examinations has no consequence
option_b: Three consecutive failures or unacceptable absence from the examination on the third occasion leads to deemed exit from the Service
option_c: Only annual leave refusal leads to exit
option_d: Only retirement age matters in all cases
correct_answer: Three consecutive failures or unacceptable absence from the examination on the third occasion leads to deemed exit from the Service
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020906 provides that three consecutive failures or unacceptable absence from promotion examination on the third occasion leads to deemed exit from the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020907, an Officer whose service is no longer required because of abolition of office shall do what?
option_a: Remain in Service indefinitely
option_b: Be required to leave the Service
correct_answer: Be required to leave the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020907, an Officer whose service is no longer required due to abolition of office is required to leave the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which of the following circumstances is covered by Rule 020907?
option_a: Re-organization of office
correct_answer: Re-organization of office
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020907 covers leaving the Service where service is no longer required due to abolition of office, re-organization of office or redundancy.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020907, redundancy may lead to what consequence?
option_a: The Officer may be required to leave the Service
option_b: The Officer must be appointed Permanent Secretary
option_c: The Officer receives automatic acting appointment
option_d: The Officer becomes exempt from PSR
correct_answer: The Officer may be required to leave the Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020907, where service is no longer required due to redundancy, the Officer is required to leave the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which option correctly lists the grounds in Rule 020907?
option_a: Abolition of office, re-organization of office or redundancy
option_b: Annual leave, sick leave and maternity leave
correct_answer: Abolition of office, re-organization of office or redundancy
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020907 provides that an Officer whose service is no longer required because of abolition of office, re-organization of office or redundancy shall leave the Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020908, what is the mandatory retirement age for all grades in the Service?
option_a: 50 years
correct_answer: 60 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020908, the mandatory retirement age for all grades in the Service is 60 years or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020908, what is the maximum pensionable service period before mandatory retirement?
option_a: 25 years
correct_answer: 35 years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020908, mandatory retirement occurs at 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which comes first for mandatory retirement under Rule 020908?
option_a: Transfer or secondment
option_c: 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service
correct_answer: 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020908, retirement is mandatory at 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: What does Rule 020908 say about remaining in Service after retirement age?
option_a: No Officer shall be allowed to remain in Service after attaining 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier
option_b: An Officer may remain indefinitely after 60 years
option_c: Only Directors may ignore the retirement age
option_d: Officers may remain if they have unused annual leave
correct_answer: No Officer shall be allowed to remain in Service after attaining 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020908, no Officer may remain in Service after attaining 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 020908 is without prejudice to prevailing conditions of service for which categories?
option_a: Judicial Officers, Academic Staff of Universities and other Officers whose retirement age differs
correct_answer: Judicial Officers, Academic Staff of Universities and other Officers whose retirement age differs
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020908, the general retirement rule is without prejudice to prevailing conditions of service for Judicial Officers, Academic Staff of Universities and other Officers whose retirement age is different.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly summarises mandatory retirement under Rule 020908?
option_a: The Service has no retirement age
option_b: All Officers retire only after 70 years
option_c: The general rule is 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier
option_d: The rule applies only to Officers on probation
correct_answer: The general rule is 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020908 provides that mandatory retirement is 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier, subject to stated exceptions.
