description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020909, when must a Director or equivalent in an MDA compulsorily retire?
option_a: After serving eight years on the post
option_b: After one year on the post
correct_answer: After serving eight years on the post
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020909, a Director or its equivalent by whatever nomenclature in MDAs shall compulsorily retire upon serving eight years on the post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 020909 applies to a Director or equivalent by whatever nomenclature in which organizations?
option_a: MDAs
correct_answer: MDAs
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020909, the eight-year tenure policy applies to a Director or equivalent by whatever nomenclature in MDAs.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020909, what is the initial term of office of a Permanent Secretary?
option_a: Four years
correct_answer: Four years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020909, a Permanent Secretary shall hold office for a term of four years.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 020909, a Permanent Secretary’s term may be renewed for what further period?
option_a: A further term of four years
option_b: A further term of ten years
option_d: A further term of one year
correct_answer: A further term of four years
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020909, a Permanent Secretary’s four-year term is renewable for a further term of four years.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Renewal of a Permanent Secretary’s term under Rule 020909 is subject to what condition?
option_a: Satisfactory performance
correct_answer: Satisfactory performance
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020909, renewal for a further term of four years is subject to satisfactory performance.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is the maximum tenure stated for a Permanent Secretary under Rule 020909?
option_a: Four years only
option_b: Four years, renewable for a further four years, and no more
correct_answer: Four years, renewable for a further four years, and no more
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 020909, a Permanent Secretary holds office for four years, renewable for a further four years subject to satisfactory performance, and no more.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects the tenure policy under Rule 020909?
option_a: Directors retire after eight years on the post, while Permanent Secretaries serve four years renewable once for another four years subject to satisfactory performance
option_b: Directors serve indefinitely, while Permanent Secretaries serve one year only
option_c: Directors must retire after two years, while Permanent Secretaries have unlimited tenure
option_d: Directors and Permanent Secretaries have no tenure limits
correct_answer: Directors retire after eight years on the post, while Permanent Secretaries serve four years renewable once for another four years subject to satisfactory performance
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 020909 provides that Directors or equivalent retire after eight years on the post, and Permanent Secretaries serve a four-year term renewable once for four years subject to satisfactory performance.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 9, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 9 of the PSR?
option_a: It regulates leaving the Service, including probationary termination, relinquishment, failure to secure confirmation, resignation, proportionate leave, exit after failing promotion examinations, abolition or redundancy, mandatory retirement and tenure policy
option_b: It deals only with annual leave abroad
option_c: It deals only with acting appointment
option_d: It regulates only medical treatment abroad
correct_answer: It regulates leaving the Service, including probationary termination, relinquishment, failure to secure confirmation, resignation, proportionate leave, exit after failing promotion examinations, abolition or redundancy, mandatory retirement and tenure policy
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 9, Rules 020901 to 020909 cover leaving the Service, including probationary termination, relinquishment during probation, failure to secure confirmation, resignation, proportionate leave, exit after failing promotion examinations, abolition of office or redundancy, mandatory retirement and tenure policy.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Under Rule 021001, which Officers must participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme?
option_a: Only contract Officers
correct_answer: All pensionable Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Chapter 2, Section 10, Rule 021001, all pensionable Officers shall participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: The Contributory Pension Scheme under Rule 021001 is provided for in which law?
option_a: Public Procurement Act, 2007
correct_answer: Pension Reform Act, 2014
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021001, participation in the Contributory Pension Scheme is as provided for in the Pension Reform Act, 2014.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Rule 021001 mainly deals with what subject?
option_a: Payment of retirement benefit
correct_answer: Payment of retirement benefit
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 021001 deals with payment of retirement benefit through participation of all pensionable Officers in the Contributory Pension Scheme.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Which statement correctly reflects Rule 021001?
option_a: Only retired Officers participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme
option_b: Only junior Officers participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme
option_c: All pensionable Officers participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme as provided by the Pension Reform Act, 2014
option_d: Contract Officers must be promoted through the Contributory Pension Scheme
correct_answer: All pensionable Officers participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme as provided by the Pension Reform Act, 2014
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021001, all pensionable Officers shall participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme as provided for in the Pension Reform Act, 2014.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Under Rule 021002, who forwards up-to-date record of service and required documents to PENCOM?
option_a: The Staff Union
correct_answer: Departmental Pension Officers
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021002, Departmental Pension Officers are required to forward up-to-date record of service and the listed documents to the Pension Commission, PENCOM.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Rule 021002 requires records and documents to be forwarded to which body?
option_a: The Pension Commission, PENCOM
correct_answer: The Pension Commission, PENCOM
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021002, Departmental Pension Officers forward the records and documents to the Pension Commission, PENCOM.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Why are Departmental Pension Officers required to forward the documents listed in Rule 021002?
option_a: To delay retirement benefit processing
option_c: To ensure Officers receive their retirement benefits promptly
correct_answer: To ensure Officers receive their retirement benefits promptly
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021002, the documents are forwarded to PENCOM in order to ensure that Officers receive their retirement benefits promptly.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 10.
question: Which document is required under Rule 021002(a)?

question: Rule 021203 is mainly concerned with what?
option_a: Duties of the person engaged
correct_answer: Duties of the person engaged
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 021203 provides for the duties of the person engaged under a non-pensionable appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021204, may the person engaged be directly or indirectly engaged in another service or business?
option_a: Yes, without restriction
option_b: Yes, if the business is profitable
option_c: No, he shall not be engaged in or concerned with any other service or business
option_d: Yes, if he informs a colleague
correct_answer: No, he shall not be engaged in or concerned with any other service or business
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021204, the person engaged shall not, directly or indirectly, be engaged in or concerned with any other service or business whatsoever.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: What does Rule 021204 say about receiving commission or profits?
option_a: The person engaged may receive commission freely
option_b: The person engaged may receive profits from any business
option_c: The person engaged may receive commission only from suppliers
option_d: The person engaged shall not receive commission or profits of any kind
correct_answer: The person engaged shall not receive commission or profits of any kind
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021204, the person engaged shall not receive commission or profits of any kind.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021204, to what must the person engaged devote his whole time and attention?
option_a: Private business
correct_answer: The Service of the Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021204, the person engaged must devote the whole of his time and attention to the Service of the Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which rules must the person engaged conform to under Rule 021204?
option_a: Public Service Rules of the Government
correct_answer: Public Service Rules of the Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021204, the person engaged shall conform to the Public Service Rules of the Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Rule 021204?
option_a: The person engaged may run any business while in Government service
option_b: The person engaged must avoid other service or business, must not receive commissions or profits, must devote full attention to Government service and must conform to the PSR
option_c: The person engaged is exempt from the PSR
option_d: The person engaged may divide official time with private employment
correct_answer: The person engaged must avoid other service or business, must not receive commissions or profits, must devote full attention to Government service and must conform to the PSR
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 021204 requires the person engaged to avoid other service or business, avoid commissions or profits, devote full time to Government service and conform to the Public Service Rules.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021205, the term “emolument” includes what where payable under the agreement?
option_a: Contract addition
correct_answer: Contract addition
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021205, “emolument” includes contract addition where this is payable under the agreement, except in Rule 021206.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 021205 states that the definition of “emolument” applies except in which rule?
option_a: Rule 021201
correct_answer: Rule 021206
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021205, the term “emolument” includes contract addition where payable, except in Rule 021206.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: From what date are increments of emoluments calculated under Rule 021205?
option_a: From the first day of the month in which the person engaged takes up appointment
option_b: From the last day of the leave year
correct_answer: From the first day of the month in which the person engaged takes up appointment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021205(i), increments of emoluments, if any, are calculated from the first day of the month in which the person engaged takes up appointment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021205, increments of emoluments shall not be granted unless what has been satisfactory?
option_a: Private business income
correct_answer: Efficiency, conduct and diligence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021205(ii), increments shall not be granted unless the efficiency, conduct and diligence of the person engaged have been satisfactory during the preceding year.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: The satisfactory efficiency, conduct and diligence required for increments under Rule 021205 must relate to what period?
option_a: The year preceding the engagement
correct_answer: The year preceding the engagement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021205(ii), increments depend on satisfactory efficiency, conduct and diligence during the year preceding the engagement.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021205, an increment shall not be withheld except on whose decision or recommendation?
option_a: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
correct_answer: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021205(ii), an increment shall not be withheld except on the decision or recommendation of the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021206, when travelling on duty away from duty post, the person engaged is subject to what?
option_a: Only his personal travel plan
option_b: Such regulations on transport and travelling allowances as Government may decide
correct_answer: Such regulations on transport and travelling allowances as Government may decide
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021206, when travelling on duty away from duty post, the person engaged is subject to Government regulations on transport and travelling allowances.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 021206 deals mainly with which subject?
option_a: Travelling allowances
correct_answer: Travelling allowances
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 021206 deals with transport and travelling allowance provisions when the person engaged travels on duty away from duty post.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who decides the applicable regulations on transport and travelling allowances under Rule 021206?
option_a: The Government
option_d: The family of the person engaged
correct_answer: The Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021206, the applicable regulations are those the Government may decide.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021207, Government pays salary due where the person engaged resigns because of what?
option_a: Ill-health not caused by his own negligence
correct_answer: Ill-health not caused by his own negligence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021207, where the person engaged is compelled by ill-health not caused by his own negligence to resign, Government pays salary due up to the relevant date.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021207, who may certify that the person engaged is incapable of rendering further efficient service?
option_a: A duly qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government
correct_answer: A duly qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021207, incapacity by infirmity of mind or body must be certified by a duly qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: The incapacity mentioned in Rule 021207 may arise from what?
option_a: Infirmity of mind or body
option_b: Failure to attend a social event
correct_answer: Infirmity of mind or body
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021207, the relevant incapacity may arise from infirmity of mind or body rendering further efficient service impossible.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Where Rule 021207 applies, salary is payable up to which date?
option_a: The date of such resignation or the date the certificate is issued
option_b: The date of first appointment only
correct_answer: The date of such resignation or the date the certificate is issued
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021207, Government pays such salary as may be due up to the date of resignation or the date on which the certificate was issued.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Which condition would prevent reliance on ill-health under Rule 021207?
option_a: Ill-health caused by the person’s own negligence
option_b: Ill-health certified by Government Healthcare Provider
correct_answer: Ill-health caused by the person’s own negligence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021207, the ill-health must not be caused by the person engaged through his own negligence.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021208, what is conclusive evidence on whether resignation was compelled by ill-health?
option_a: A certificate of Medical Fitness duly signed by a qualified Government Healthcare Provider
option_b: A private letter from a colleague
correct_answer: A certificate of Medical Fitness duly signed by a qualified Government Healthcare Provider
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021208, a certificate of Medical Fitness duly signed by a qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government is conclusive evidence on whether resignation was compelled by ill-health.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Who must sign the certificate of Medical Fitness under Rule 021208?
option_a: A qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government
correct_answer: A qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021208, the certificate must be signed by a qualified Healthcare Provider employed by the Government.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 1 of 2.
question: Rule 021208 is used to determine what question?
option_a: Whether the person engaged was compelled to resign by reason of ill-health
option_b: Whether the person engaged is due for promotion
option_c: Whether the person engaged should receive transport allowance
option_d: Whether the person engaged may join another business
correct_answer: Whether the person engaged was compelled to resign by reason of ill-health
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021208, the certificate is conclusive evidence on whether the person engaged was compelled to resign by reason of ill-health.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021209, Government may dismiss the person engaged if he does what?
option_a: Neglects or refuses to perform duties or comply with any order
correct_answer: Neglects or refuses to perform duties or comply with any order
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021209, Government may dismiss the person engaged if he neglects or refuses to perform duties or comply with any order.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which exception is recognized under Rule 021209 where the person is unable to perform duties?
option_a: Ill-health not caused by his own negligence
correct_answer: Ill-health not caused by his own negligence
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021209, inability to perform duties may be excused only where it is due to ill-health not caused by the person’s own negligence.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021209, disclosure of Government affairs to whom may lead to dismissal?
option_a: An unauthorized person
correct_answer: An unauthorized person
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021209, disclosure of information in respect of Government affairs to any unauthorized person may lead to dismissal.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021209, what happens to rights and privileges accrued under the agreement upon dismissal?
option_a: They cease
option_d: They are transferred to the Staff Union
correct_answer: They cease
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021209, upon dismissal, all rights and privileges accrued to the person engaged by the agreement shall cease.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Rule 021209?
option_a: Government may dismiss the person engaged for neglect, refusal of duty, failure to comply with orders, unauthorized disclosure or misconduct, and accrued rights and privileges cease
option_b: Government cannot dismiss a non-pensionable appointee
option_c: Government may dismiss only after retirement
correct_answer: Government may dismiss the person engaged for neglect, refusal of duty, failure to comply with orders, unauthorized disclosure or misconduct, and accrued rights and privileges cease
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 021209 allows dismissal for neglect, refusal of duty, failure to comply with orders, unauthorized disclosure or misconduct, and provides that accrued rights and privileges under the agreement cease upon dismissal.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021210, Government may terminate the engagement by giving what notice?
option_a: Three months’ notice in writing
correct_answer: Three months’ notice in writing
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021210(i), Government may terminate the engagement by giving three months’ notice in writing.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Instead of giving three months’ notice, what may Government pay under Rule 021210?
option_a: One month’s salary in lieu of notice
correct_answer: One month’s salary in lieu of notice
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021210(i), Government may terminate by giving three months’ notice in writing or by paying one month’s salary in lieu of notice.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: After what period of service may the person engaged terminate his engagement under Rule 021210?
option_a: After expiration of three months of service
correct_answer: After expiration of three months of service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021210(ii), the person engaged may terminate his engagement at any time after the expiration of three months of service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: How may the person engaged terminate his engagement after three months of service under Rule 021210?
option_a: By giving Government three months’ notice in writing or paying Government one month’s salary in lieu of notice
option_b: By sending a verbal message to a colleague
correct_answer: By giving Government three months’ notice in writing or paying Government one month’s salary in lieu of notice
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021210(ii), the person engaged may terminate by giving Government three months’ notice in writing or paying Government one month’s salary in lieu of notice.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly reflects termination under Rule 021210?
option_a: Both Government and the person engaged have notice or salary-in-lieu options under the rule
option_b: Only the Staff Union may terminate the engagement
option_c: The person engaged can terminate only after retirement
option_d: Government must always give one year’s notice
correct_answer: Both Government and the person engaged have notice or salary-in-lieu options under the rule
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021210, Government may terminate by three months’ written notice or one month’s salary in lieu, and the person engaged may also terminate after three months’ service by three months’ written notice or one month’s salary in lieu.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021211, pecuniary damage may arise from disregarding or failing to comply with what?
option_a: Any order, standing order or departmental instruction
correct_answer: Any order, standing order or departmental instruction
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021211, pecuniary damage may arise from disregarding or failing to comply with any order, standing order or departmental instruction, or from neglect of duty.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021211, pecuniary damage may also arise from what on the part of the person engaged?
option_a: Neglect of duty
correct_answer: Neglect of duty
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021211, pecuniary damage arising from neglect of duty may make the person engaged liable to salary deduction.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: What may be deducted under Rule 021211 to make good pecuniary damage?
option_a: Salary of the person engaged
correct_answer: Salary of the person engaged
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021211, the person engaged may be liable to a deduction from salary to make good the damage or part of it.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Who fixes the amount to be deducted for pecuniary damage under Rule 021211?
option_a: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
correct_answer: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021211, the amount to be deducted is fixed by the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021212, when must the person engaged give written notice if he desires to remain in Government employment?
option_a: Four months before the date of expiration of the agreement
correct_answer: Four months before the date of expiration of the agreement
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021212, four months before the expiration of the agreement, the person engaged must give written notice to Government stating his desire to remain in employment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: The written notice under Rule 021212 states what?
option_a: The desire to remain in Government employment
option_c: The desire to avoid the PSR
option_d: The desire to disclose Government information
correct_answer: The desire to remain in Government employment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021212, the written notice must state the person’s desire to remain in Government employment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: After receiving the notice under Rule 021212, what does Government decide?
option_a: Whether it will offer further employment
option_b: Whether to grant maternity leave only
option_d: Whether to promote the Staff Union
correct_answer: Whether it will offer further employment
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021212, Government decides whether it will offer the person engaged further employment.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: If Government decides in favour of further employment under Rule 021212, re-engagement shall be on what basis?
option_a: Such terms and for such period as may be mutually agreed
correct_answer: Such terms and for such period as may be mutually agreed
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021212, if Government decides in favour, re-engagement is on such terms and for such period as may be mutually agreed.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021213, when is the person engaged eligible for severance allowance?
option_a: On satisfactory completion of a tour of service
option_d: On unauthorized disclosure of Government information
correct_answer: On satisfactory completion of a tour of service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021213, the person engaged is eligible for severance allowance on satisfactory completion of a tour of service, subject to the stated conditions.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: What is the severance allowance rate under Rule 021213?
option_a: 15 percent of basic salary
correct_answer: 15 percent of basic salary
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021213, severance allowance is payable at the rate of 15 percent of basic salary.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021213, severance allowance is not payable if the engagement is terminated under which rule?
option_a: Rule 021210
correct_answer: Rule 021210
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021213, severance allowance is payable only if the engagement is not terminated as under Rule 021210.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which further condition affects eligibility for severance allowance under Rule 021213?
option_a: The person engaged must not be in receipt of, or eligible for, any other retiring benefits
option_b: The person engaged must be a Staff Union officer
option_c: The person engaged must have refused all duties
option_d: The person engaged must have disclosed Government information
correct_answer: The person engaged must not be in receipt of, or eligible for, any other retiring benefits
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021213, severance allowance is payable only if the person engaged is not in receipt of, nor eligible for, any other retiring benefits.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement correctly summarises Rule 021213?
option_a: Severance allowance is 15 percent of basic salary on satisfactory completion of tour, provided the engagement was not terminated under Rule 021210 and no other retiring benefit is received or receivable
option_b: Severance allowance is automatic after dismissal
option_c: Severance allowance is paid only to pensionable Officers
option_d: Severance allowance is always 100 percent of salary
correct_answer: Severance allowance is 15 percent of basic salary on satisfactory completion of tour, provided the engagement was not terminated under Rule 021210 and no other retiring benefit is received or receivable
feedback: Correct. PSR Rule 021213 provides for severance allowance at 15 percent of basic salary on satisfactory completion of a tour of service, provided the engagement was not terminated under Rule 021210 and the person is not receiving or eligible for other retiring benefits.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021214, is leave of absence a legal right included in the contract?
option_a: Yes, it is an automatic legal right
option_b: No, it is not a legal right included in the contract
option_c: Yes, but only for senior Officers
correct_answer: No, it is not a legal right included in the contract
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021214, leave of absence is not a legal right included in the contract.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021214, leave may be granted after which event?
option_a: After a tour of service
correct_answer: After a tour of service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021214, leave may be granted after a tour of service, subject to the applicable rules and exigencies of the Public Service.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Under Rule 021214, leave may also be granted if the person engaged is declared what before completing the tour?
option_a: Invalid
correct_answer: Invalid
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021214, leave may be granted if the person engaged is declared invalid before completing the tour.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Rule 021214 also allows leave where the engagement is terminated by reason of ill-health in accordance with which rule?
option_a: Rule 021207
correct_answer: Rule 021207
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021214, leave may be granted where the engagement is terminated by reason of ill-health in accordance with Rule 021207.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Where leave is granted under Rule 021214, the applicable rules are those for whom?
option_a: Nigerian Officers of a similar grade level
correct_answer: Nigerian Officers of a similar grade level
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021214, leave may be granted under rules applicable to Nigerian Officers of a similar grade level.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Leave under Rule 021214 is granted subject to what?
option_a: Exigencies of the Public Service
correct_answer: Exigencies of the Public Service
feedback: Correct. Under PSR Rule 021214, leave may be granted so far as exigencies of the Public Service permit.

description: Public Service Rules Chapter 2 practice quiz. Section 12, Part 2 of 2.
question: Which statement best summarises Chapter 2, Section 12 of the PSR?
option_a: It regulates the schedule for non-pensionable appointment, including term, duties, PSR conformity, emoluments, travel, ill-health, dismissal, termination, liability, further employment, severance allowance and leave
option_b: It deals only with promotion examinations
option_c: It deals only with mandatory pension contribution
option_d: It deals only with Certificate of Service
correct_answer: It regulates the schedule for non-pensionable appointment, including term, duties, PSR conformity, emoluments, travel, ill-health, dismissal, termination, liability, further employment, severance allowance and leave
feedback: Correct. PSR Chapter 2, Section 12, Rules 021201 to 021214 regulate the schedule for non-pensionable appointment, covering term of engagement, completion of term, duties, conformity to PSR, emoluments, travelling allowances, ill-health, medical fitness certificate, dismissal, termination, liability for damage, further employment, severance allowance and leave.
